Special behaviors: Cannot be deleted if in use (application-level rule).

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Parent category id {@link product_categories.id} (for hierarchy); nullable for root.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category display name; atomic. E.g.: 'Apparel', 'Running Shoes'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Category creation timestamp, for logging, evidence, and i18n flows.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Category update timestamp. Maintains audit/compliance.

models.name: product_options
models.description:
Product option entity - Implements products' option normalization requirement.

Represents a single specifiable option (e.g., color, size) for use in variants. Maintains full 3NF by keeping every atomic choice as a separate record, variants reference these options. For example: 'Color: Red', 'Size: 10'.

Key relationships: many-to-many with product_variants via join table, belongs to a product.
Special behaviors: Option values are language-agnostic and referenced. No calculated in-option fields.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique product option identifier.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Owns product's {@link products.id} - Each option is scoped to a single product.

plainFields.name: option_type
plainFields.description: Type of option (e.g., 'color', 'size'). Atomic descriptor, no list aggregation.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Atomic option value (e.g., 'Red', 'XL'). Single value per record; reference only.

models.name: product_tags
models.description:
Product tag entity - This implements the tagging requirement, supporting extensible and AI-generated tags for search/discovery.

Represents a single logical tag, maintained fully normalized (one tag per record). Used for many-to-many linking to products via a junction; enables advanced AI/ML. E.g., 'Eco-friendly', 'AI-generated: trending', '2025 Spring'.

Key relationships: many-to-many with products via join table. Not bound to product for de-dupe.
Special behaviors: Cannot be deleted if mapped to product by business rule (handled in logic, not schema).

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Atomic tag value: presented for searches, filtering, and AI workflows. Not compound fields. E.g., 'Seasonal'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for tag creation; enables audit, compliance, and ML features.

models.name: product_media
models.description:
Product media entity - Implements digital asset management for products, normalization requirement for file/asset reference.

Represents a single atomic asset—image, video, PDF—linked to a product or variant. Asset metadata and localization handled at field level. Maintains normalization by not duplicating media data. E.g., 'main.jpg', 'unboxing.mp4'.

Key relationships: linked to product or product_variant, not both. Media may be globally reused via indirect links.
Special behaviors: File content is reference only (URI), not stored in DB.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Linked product's {@link products.id}. Exactly one of product_id or product_variant_id must be non-null.

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Linked product variant's {@link product_variants.id}. Enforces exclusivity, one of two FK must be set.

plainFields.name: uri
plainFields.description: Atomic URI to remote asset (never stores blobs in DB).

plainFields.name: media_type
plainFields.description: Type of asset ('image', 'video', etc).

plainFields.name: locale
plainFields.description: Locale/region of this asset, per i18n/a11y. E.g.: 'ko-KR'.

plainFields.name: alt_text
plainFields.description: Accessibility alt text for asset, complying with a11y WCA2.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Asset creation timestamp; audit/evidence field, 3NF.

models.name: inventory
models.description:
Inventory entity - Implements core inventory tracking and evidence preservation requirement.

Represents a normalized, atomic inventory record for product variants. No aggregate or pre-computed stock. Maintains 3NF by keeping each update/event in a separate record (history by design). For example: inventory for 'Nike Air Max 2025, Size 10'.

Key relationships: One-to-one links with product_variant; ties to evidence/events for audit. 
Special behaviors: never calculates stock at DB layer—only raw stock updates and absolute counts.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique inventory record identifier.

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Tracked variant's {@link product_variants.id}. Each inventory maps to exactly one variant.

plainFields.name: stock_count
plainFields.description: Current available quantity of the variant, stored as absolute number. No pre-calculation or aggregate fields (only most recent state, all log/events via catalog_event).

plainFields.name: last_modified_at
plainFields.description: Last update time to this inventory; compliance and event tracking, atomic.

models.name: import_feeds
models.description:
Import feed entity - Implements catalog import normalization and data provenance requirement.

Represents an atomic, external data feed used for catalog enrichment/import tracking. Maintains 3NF, links each imported product/variant via foreign key. For example: Google Shopping product import, partner ERP feed.

Key relationships: product_variant is mapped to a single import_feed.
Special behaviors: mutable for correction, immutable evidence via catalog_evidence. No calculated aggregate fields allowed.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique import feed identifier.

plainFields.name: source_name
plainFields.description: Human-readable name of the import source. E.g., 'Google Shopping'.

plainFields.name: source_uri
plainFields.description: URI of the import data source/feed; allows for evidence and provenance tracking.

plainFields.name: imported_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of data feed import into catalog; audit/compliance.

models.name: catalog_events
models.description:
Catalog event entity - Implements catalog state change logging, compliance, and evidence preservation requirement.

Represents an immutable, atomic event: product/variant creation, change, import, status update, etc. Maintains strict normalization (no denormalized rollup in this table), links to evidence and actors. For example: a price update event for a variant.

Key relationships: links user (actor), product or variant, optional evidence pointer.
Special behaviors: Chronological, append-only; never updated/deleted.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Target product's {@link products.id}. Nullable, may target variant instead.

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Target variant's {@link product_variants.id}. Nullable if product-level event.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Responsible actor's {@link users.id} (who performed the event).

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Type of event (e.g., creation, update, import, deletion, status_change, etc). Atomic category (not compound).

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of event for compliance/evidence. Atomic; not calculated.

plainFields.name: occurred_at
plainFields.description: Atomic timestamp of event occurrence. Preserves chronological evidence and supports full audit trail.

models.name: catalog_evidence
models.description:
Catalog evidence entity - Implements immutable evidence preservation requirement for all critical catalog actions/events per compliance rules.

Represents a single, atomic evidence/log record attached to an event: file links, signature, or raw snapshot URI. Maintains strict normalization; links to catalog_event or catalog-related entity. For example: file hash of import, signed docs for regulatory purposes.

Key relationships: links to at most one catalog_event, may be referenced by compliance/external audit logic.
Special behaviors: Direct evidence content never stored; only signed reference/URI.

foreignFields.name: catalog_event_id
foreignFields.description: Target event's {@link catalog_events.id}. Each evidence strictly linked to one event per 3NF, nullable for external evidence.

plainFields.name: reference_uri
plainFields.description: Atomic URI (file, s3, IPFS, hash url, etc) to external evidence; never locally stored blobs.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Atomic evidence description for traceability and legal compliance.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Evidence creation timestamp; 3NF compliance, chronological audit.

models.name: cart
models.description:
[Cart management] - This implements the requirement for intelligent, audit-preserving cart management from the 'Intelligent Cart and Order Processing Requirements Specification'.

This model represents a user's persistent cart, maintaining strict data integrity, full auditability, session support, and secure linkage to user or session. It ensures 3NF normalization by keeping only atomic and essential cart-level data; item-level details reside in cart_item. Example: recovering a user's cart across multiple devices or after authentication.

Key relationships: references user, session, and cart_item models for ownership, context, and item containment.
Special behaviors: Cart identity is unique; maintains only normalized relations, all item data tracked via junction table.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Identifies each cart instance uniquely.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description:
Belonged user's {@link users.id}
The primary account associated with this cart; enables cart persistence across devices and sessions.

foreignFields.name: session_id
foreignFields.description:
Associated session's {@link sessions.id}
Optional. Associates anonymous/pre-login carts; provides seamless upgrade upon login.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Cart creation timestamp] - Implements evidence and regulatory requirements. Used for audit logging, recovery, and analytics. Ensures normalization by tracking atomic event only. Ex: '2025-06-10T04:59:24' when cart first initiated.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Cart update timestamp] - Implements traceability and audit requirements, storing only atomic last-changed value. Allows tracking of recent activity. Ex: '2025-06-10T05:03:45' after a product added.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: [Soft deletion timestamp] - Implements compliance, right-to-be-forgotten, and data integrity requirements. Null if active, set on removal for evidence trail. Ex: null for active, timestamp for deleted cart.

models.name: cart_item
models.description:
[Cart item detail] - This implements the requirement for normalized, auditable cart item management from the 'Intelligent Cart and Order Processing Requirements Specification'.

Represents each item in a user's cart, maintaining full normalization (3NF). Item quantities, variant choice, and intent are recorded atomically. Auditability is ensured by timestamping and separate evidence models where required. Example: when a user adds three units of a size-M, green T-shirt variant to cart.

Key relationships: references cart, product_variant for linkage; product reference maintained via product_variant only. No calculated data; all denormalization only in views.
Special behaviors: One cart_item per variant per cart; unique constraint enforced.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies this cart-item record.

foreignFields.name: cart_id
foreignFields.description:
Parent cart's {@link cart.id}
Links this item to the cart that holds it.

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description:
Product variant's {@link product_variants.id}
Links to the specific SKU/configuration the user intends to buy.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: [Quantity desired] - Implements cart quantity requirements. Stores atomic, user-specified intent. Ex: '3' for three items of the variant.

plainFields.name: added_at
plainFields.description: [Item addition timestamp] - Serves evidence and analytics needs. Timestamp for when specific item added to cart. Ex: '2025-06-10T04:59:24'.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Last update timestamp] - Tracks modification; e.g. quantity update. Normalized (not derived) atomic history. Ex: '2025-06-10T05:00:00'.

models.name: order
models.description:
[Order lifecycle record] - Implements the requirement for normalized, robust, evidence-preserving order process management from the requirements specification.

Each order record represents a unique commerce transaction, including linkage to user, cart, payment, and state tracking. Strict 3NF assures no duplication—order_items contain line-level details. All status/history/evidence handled via related tables. Example: new purchase by user, tracked through all subsequent states (placed, shipped, completed).

Key relationships: references user, cart, payment and state-tracking models for full join capability.
Special behaviors: Atomic values only (total, status, etc. never pre-calculated). Order evidence and logs stored externally for compliance.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique ID per order transaction.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description:
Ordering user's {@link users.id}
Links order to user account for audit and analytics.

foreignFields.name: cart_id
foreignFields.description:
Source cart's {@link cart.id}
Links to the cart used to place this order. Enables full evidence chain for compliance.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Order creation timestamp] - Required by audit, compliance, and analytics. Atomic, strictly non-duplicated event. E.g., '2025-06-10T04:59:24'.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Order update timestamp] - Captures atomic change events for evidence and operational review. E.g., '2025-06-10T05:30:00'.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: [Soft delete marker] - For compliance and historic evidence, set if order is voided/cancelled; otherwise null. Never physically deleted.

models.name: order_item
models.description:
[Order line-level detail] - Implements the requirement for strictly normalized, traceable order item management.

Represents each SKU/configuration in an order, recording atomic quantity and reference to product_variant. Ensures full 3NF by detaching all calculations, price, or analytic rollup. All audit trails and evidence for each action reside in related tables. Example: order includes 2 blue jeans, variant #7.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for line item.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description:
Parent order's {@link order.id}
Links to the order containing this line item.

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description:
Product variant's {@link product_variants.id}
Spell out the line as describing which exact stock-keeping unit.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: [Ordered quantity] - Stores user-purchased units. Ensures atomic, normalized order content. E.g., user orders 2 of variant #7.

plainFields.name: added_at
plainFields.description: [Addition to order timestamp] - For evidence and tracking requirements. Details time when item became part of order. E.g., '2025-06-10T04:59:24'.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Update timestamp] - For last atomic update to line item details. For event logging. E.g., '2025-06-10T05:04:03'.

models.name: order_status
models.description:
[Order status tracking] - Implements normalized, evidence-enabled order lifecycle state management as required for audit, analytics, and compliance.

Each record logs a status transition for an order, rather than storing 'latest' status inline. Full history of order state is tracked as a sequence by timestamps. Example: 'pending', 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered'.

Key relationships: references order for parent linkage.
Special behaviors: No denormalization; only atomic status per row. Materialized views to hold summary/latest states.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. One per status change event.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description:
Target order's {@link order.id}
Defines which order this status record is about.

plainFields.name: status_code
plainFields.description: [Order status code] - Represents atomic order state (e.g., 'pending', 'paid', 'shipped'). Compliance: values are strictly controlled by system logic or enumeration.

plainFields.name: changed_at
plainFields.description: [Status change timestamp] - Implements complete event history. Atomic per change. E.g., '2025-06-10T05:12:09'.

plainFields.name: changed_by
plainFields.description: [Status changer] - For evidence and audit, identifies the user or system actor triggering the state change. Links to user.id or reserved system id. Null if system-automated.

models.name: order_log
models.description:
[Order event logging] - Implements the requirement for immutable, tamper-evident record of all material order-related actions.

Each record logs an event (e.g., creation, update, state transition, evidence attachment) for an order, including timestamps and relevant actor info. All analytics, AI-driven detection, and compliance evidence are sourced from this log. Full 3NF compliance is achieved—no calculated or summary fields.

Key relationships: references target order; may reference evidence where applicable.
Special behaviors: Immutable logs; complete itemization (no aggregations within table).

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description:
Target order's {@link order.id}
Order event relates to this specific transaction.

foreignFields.name: evidence_id
foreignFields.description:
Linked evidence's {@link order_evidence.id}
Optional; logs external file or digital signature as audit evidence for this event.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: [Event type] - Type or category of event; e.g., 'create', 'update', 'status_change', 'attach_evidence'. Normalized, not pre-calculated. Used for filtering, audit, analytics.

plainFields.name: event_description
plainFields.description: [Event detail] - Atomic description, not derived or aggregated. E.g., 'Order was shipped via courier'.

plainFields.name: event_time
plainFields.description: [Event timestamp] - Exact time when event occurred; essential for evidence compliance and analytics.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: [Event actor] - User ID or system actor responsible for event. Used in compliance analysis. Null if unauthenticated or system auto-action.

models.name: order_evidence
models.description:
[Order evidence registry] - Satisfies requirement to record all compliance, audit or dispute evidence associated with order operations.

Holds atomic pointers to files, digital receipts, or cryptographic proof objects related to a specific order. Evidence records are separate for full normalization. Example: PDF invoice, delivery photo, digital signature pertaining to an order.

Key relationships: links order and potentially the user or system actor providing the evidence.
Special behaviors: Only atomic and external reference fields allowed; all denormalization in materialized view.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description:
Associated order's {@link order.id}
Defines which order this evidence relates to.

plainFields.name: evidence_type
plainFields.description: [Evidence type] - Type of evidence (e.g., 'invoice', 'signature', 'photo', 'receipt'). Normalized, strictly conformance for evidence audit. E.g., 'invoice'.

plainFields.name: evidence_uri
plainFields.description: [Evidence URI] - URI/location to external asset or file. Atomic, not aggregated. E.g., 'https://evidence.bucket/signed-invoice.pdf'.

plainFields.name: provided_at
plainFields.description: [Provided timestamp] - When the evidence was recorded into the system. Serves compliance and analytics. E.g., '2025-06-10T06:09:00'.

plainFields.name: provided_by
plainFields.description: [Provider/actor reference] - User or third-party id responsible for provision. For traceability, audit and compliance. Null if system-automated.

models.name: payments
models.description:
[Payment Record] - This implements the recording of all monetary operations from the requirements analysis, specifically the 'secure, traceable, and compliant payment operations' and 'transaction integrity' points under AI-Driven Discount & Payment Systems. 

Maintains 3NF by separating atomic payment data from aggregated/AI-inferred outcomes. For example, each payment event (checkout, refund, wallet top-up) is represented as a unique entry, providing a clear evidence trail.

Key relationships: payment_methods for source, transactions as the business event driver, user linkage for payer/payee integrity. 
Special behaviors: immutable record post-creation (all changes are audited by payment_audit), PCI compliance enforced by business logic.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each payment record.

foreignFields.name: transaction_id
foreignFields.description: Linked transaction's {@link transactions.id}. Connects the payment to its parent business event for traceability and reconciliation.

foreignFields.name: payment_method_id
foreignFields.description: Payment method's {@link payment_methods.id}. Specifies the method used for this payment (credit card, wallet, etc).

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: [Monetary amount] - Implements the requirement for accurate financial ledger. The value of this payment, always positive. Maintains atomicity for compliance and analytics. For example, a purchase worth $99.99 or partial refund of $10.00.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: [Currency code] - Implements multi-currency/locale requirement. 3-letter ISO code, e.g., USD, KRW, EUR. Normalized to prevent code confusion. Used for all reporting and conversions.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: [Payment status] - Implements lifecycle & auditability requirement. Values: pending, completed, failed, refunded, held, etc. Atomic by being tracked per payment; end-to-end state traces go to payment_audit table.

plainFields.name: initiated_at
plainFields.description: [Initiation timestamp] - Implements evidence preservation and audit trail. The moment this payment operation (attempt) was started. Always set at record creation. Used for forensic traceability.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: [Completion timestamp] - For state transition/tracking requirement. The moment the payment succeeded/failed. Nullable when pending. Used in compliance/reconciliation.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: [Optional payment description] - Business-facing note or payment memo. Implements requirement for evidence context/supporting documentation; not mandatory for atomicity.

models.name: payment_methods
models.description:
[Payment Method Catalog] - Implements the requirement for modular payment method extensibility in the Payment System Architecture section. Manages all user-supported and 3rd-party payment instruments.

Maintains 3NF by storing atomic payment instrument data for each logical method (e.g., credit card, wallet, crypto account), avoiding redundancy and storing no aggregated fields. For example, a user might have multiple cards and wallets associated here.

Key relationships: Used by payments, referenced by vouchers or campaigns. Special behaviors: supports inactivation rather than deletion for evidence preservation and ongoing compliance.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the payment method.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged user's {@link users.id}. Which user owns or registers this payment method.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: [Payment method type] - Required for payment routing and compliance logic. E.g., VISA, Mastercard, PayPal, Internal Wallet, Crypto. Normalized to keep atomic per-method information. For example, prevents inconsistent labels.

plainFields.name: masked_detail
plainFields.description: [Masked display field] - Implements PCI compliance and business UI logic for safe display. Stores last N digits or partial ID, never sensitive data. Maintains atomicity. For example, 4242 for a VISA card, 0xAb... for wallet.

plainFields.name: provider
plainFields.description: [Provider/source platform] - For extensible payment rails and auditability. Not always present (e.g., direct bank transfer). Records vendor for reconciliation. Example: Toss, Stripe, Binance.

plainFields.name: active
plainFields.description: [Activation flag] - Maintains audit/evidence requirements for never deleting payment methods. Only inactive if revoked/expired/deregistered. Required for evidence compliance.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Creation timestamp] - For audit trail and evidence preservation. Set on method entry record creation. Used in reporting and compliance.

models.name: discounts
models.description:
[Discount Record] - Implements logical representation of all discounts applied within the system, as required for 'auditable, traceable, and AI-driven discounting' in the requirements. Records only atomic logic, with all calculations performed at runtime or in materialized views.

Maintains 3NF by separating discount logic/ref into discount_rules. Applied discounts per order or item reference this table, never storing totalled values except via linkage.

Key relationships: discount_rules, orders; special behaviors: immutable after application, with all changes logged via payment_audit.

foreignFields.name: discount_rule_id
foreignFields.description: Linked rule's {@link discount_rules.id}. The rule which provides the logic for this discount entry.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Target order's {@link order.id}. The order benefiting from this discount.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: [Discount value] - Implements the requirement for capturing exact benefit conferred, with atomic record of the numerical value (always negative or 0). Maintains normalization and enables reconciliation/audit. For example, -5.00 for a $5 discount.

plainFields.name: applied_at
plainFields.description: [Time of application] - Required for audit/evidence, records when the discount was actually attached to the order.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: [Discount notes/context] - Implements requirement for transparency and traceability, e.g. which campaign, customer, or business rule applied. Atomic, optional.

models.name: discount_rules
models.description:
[Discount Rule Registry] - Implements modular management of discount logic for the Discount & Payment Core. Records normalized, AI/model-driven or administrator-created discount strategies, never the calculated results. Fulfills the requirement to maintain audit-ready, explainable, and reusable discount rule definitions.

3NF maintained by isolating parameters, such as type, amount, configuration, and referencing origin (e.g., campaign, voucher).

Key relationships: discount_campaigns as creators/assigners. Used by discounts. Special: deactivation for audit purposes; can reference AI model versions if used for A/B or ML-discounting.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the discount rule.

foreignFields.name: campaign_id
foreignFields.description: Discount campaign's {@link discount_campaigns.id}. The campaign associated with this rule for aggregation and analytics.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: [Rule type] - Required for runtime discounting. Configurable value (e.g., 'percentage', 'fixed', 'bogo', 'ml-model', etc). Enforces rule-driven modularity. Example: 'percentage' or 'dynamic-ai'.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: [Rule value] - Stores the core numeric for the discount computation (e.g., 20.0 for a 20% rule, 10.00 for $10 fixed). Maintains 3NF.

plainFields.name: active
plainFields.description: [Activation flag] - If false, this rule is archived/disabled but included for evidence. Implements requirement for rule lifecycles and traceable config change.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Creation timestamp] - Maintains audit and compliance. For example, date when administrator or AI model created this rule.

plainFields.name: ai_model_version_id
plainFields.description: [AI Model Version] - Links to {@link ai_model_versions.id} if this rule is generated or managed by a specific AI/ML model version (for explainability, audit).

models.name: discount_campaigns
models.description:
[Discount Campaign Definition] - Implements requirements for campaign lifecycle, auditability, modular campaign-based discounting. Design allows grouping/analytics over a series of discounts and their rules.

Maintains full normalization by separating campaign attributes (name, time, status) from rule application.

Key relationships: discount_rules (rules), referenced from discounts/carts/orders. Special: can be deactivated but never deleted, and includes event evidence for traceability.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: [Campaign name] - Req. for grouping and operator reporting (e.g. Black Friday 2025). Atomic and normalized.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: [Campaign description] - Optional context and business notes (e.g. rules, partners). Maintains auditability.

plainFields.name: start_at
plainFields.description: [Start time] - Implements evidence/traceability. When this campaign becomes active for discount rule matching. Maintains normalization.

plainFields.name: end_at
plainFields.description: [End time] - Campaign end date for reporting and eligibility. Used in audits and regulatory logs. Nullable for open campaigns.

plainFields.name: active
plainFields.description: [Campaign active flag] - If false, campaign is archived and no longer matchable. Maintains evidence, 3NF, and compliance.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Campaign creation timestamp] - Required for audit trail, reporting, and evidence. Set at insertion, not updated.

models.name: transactions
models.description:
[Transaction Master Record] - Fulfills the requirement that every business event causing a payment has a single, evidence-preserving, auditable record. Maintains 3NF by holding one row per transaction event (e.g. an order checkout, a wallet top-up) and separating linked payments, refunds, and discounts into their own tables.

Key relationships: Reference to orders, user. Special behaviors: immutable once recorded except notes (audited by payment_audit table), all monetary activity references a transaction id.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Represents the unique identifier for each transaction event.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Transaction initiator's {@link users.id}. Links actions to specific identity for audit, fraud prevention, and analytics.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Linked order's {@link order.id}. Which order or business event this transaction is for (or null for wallet loads, standalone events).

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: [Transaction type] - Required, fulfills compliance for event classification (e.g. purchase, refund, credit, debit, wallet-topup). Enforces analytics/audit requirements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Event time] - Start time of the business event, fulfills evidence requirements and enables chronological reconstruction.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: [Business event memo/description] - Optional context for reporting, audit, or customer support.

models.name: vouchers
models.description:
[Voucher/Loyalty Asset] - Implements the requirement for voucher, gift card, or pre-purchased credit support. Each is tracked as an independent asset, enabling compliance with prepaid, gift, refund, or promotional voucher flows.

Maintains atomic record per voucher, with lifecycle tracking for issuance, redemption, audit trail on all changes. Never deleted for evidence.

Key relationships: users (owner), payment_methods (if method-specific/voucher activation/restriction applies), campaign (for analytics/tracking), orders (redemption). Special: evidence chain for regulatory compliance.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Voucher owner's {@link users.id}. For gift/asset transfer or loyalty programs.

foreignFields.name: campaign_id
foreignFields.description: Issuing campaign's {@link discount_campaigns.id}. For business tracking and analytics integration.

foreignFields.name: payment_method_id
foreignFields.description: Payment method constraint's {@link payment_methods.id} (optional). Restricts redemption to method (e.g. in-app, crypto, external card).

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: [Voucher code] - Unique, human-readable alphanumeric. Implements redemption security and audit; not a calculated field. For example: GIFT-2024-JANE-XYZ.

plainFields.name: balance
plainFields.description: [Current amount] - The exact value (at issue or updated on use) remaining on this voucher. Edited only through auditable operations. Maintains 3NF. Example: 50.00 for $50 voucher.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: [Voucher currency] - 3-letter ISO code; enforces multicurrency design and compliance. E.g., USD, EUR.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: [Expiration date] - Timestamp when voucher becomes invalid. Nullable for non-expiring. Satisfies compliance for customer comms and refunds.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Asset issue timestamp] - When voucher assigned or loaded. Enforced as immutable. Maintains audit.

plainFields.name: redeemed_at
plainFields.description: [Redemption/usage timestamp] - If voucher is single-use or depleted. Nullable for as-yet-unredeemed codes. Maintains normalization.

models.name: loyalty_points
models.description:
[Loyalty Points Ledger] - Implements loyalty programs per requirements, ensuring all point accruals/deductions are atomic, traceable, and normalized. Directly supports point-of-sale, campaign, and retroactive benefit application via reference to user/event/campaign.

Maintains one record per transaction/event (3NF), while summaries and analytics are computed in materialized views only.

Key relationships: users (owner), transactions (origin event), campaigns (linked context), referenced in rewards, discounts.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique loyalty points ledger entry.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Points holder's {@link users.id}. Matches accrual/deduction to the beneficiary of points.

foreignFields.name: transaction_id
foreignFields.description: Origin transaction's {@link transactions.id}. Details which business event granted/used points.

foreignFields.name: campaign_id
foreignFields.description: Linked campaign's {@link discount_campaigns.id}, if any, for analytics. Nullable when directly earned (e.g. referral, review).

plainFields.name: points
plainFields.description: [Points value] - Exact points earned/spent in this event. Always positive or negative, never calculated field. Example: 10.0 earned on purchase, -5.0 for redemption.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: [Points event type] - Required for analytics and business reporting. E.g., 'earn', 'redeem', 'bonus', 'expire'. Atomic and normalized.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Ledger event timestamp] - Required for evidence and compliance; tracks the atomic moment of this points event.

models.name: refunds
models.description:
[Refund Record] - Fulfills traceable, auditable refund flows for partial or full payments, applying to the PCI-regulated payment and order flows. Normalized to one row per refund event, with order, payment, and transaction references as applicable.

All refund calculations/aggregates are to be computed in views. 3NF maintained by only storing atomic per-operation data.

Key relationships: payments (source), transactions (business event), orders (context). Special: always documented in payment_audit for compliance and evidence.

foreignFields.name: payment_id
foreignFields.description: Refunds original payment's {@link payments.id}. Traceable, required for audit and compliance.

foreignFields.name: transaction_id
foreignFields.description: Business event's {@link transactions.id}. The transaction driving this refund (for evidence chain and aggregation).

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Relevant order's {@link order.id}. Context for reporting, analytics, and recovery; nullable for standalone refunds. Fulfills regulatory traceability.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: [Refund amount] - Atomic per-refund event (no aggregate). Value refunded in currency. Maintains audit and evidence, supports negative for chargebacks.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: [Currency code] - Enforces multi-currency design; matches payment/order context. 3-letter ISO code.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: [Refund status] - Completes state machine for audit/compliance (e.g., requested, processed, rejected, completed). Always atomic; tracked for evidence.

plainFields.name: requested_at
plainFields.description: [Request timestamp] - When refund request was filed. Atomic for evidence chain and customer service trace. Set at creation.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: [Completion timestamp] - When refund finalized. Nullable for pending/cancelled. Maintains compliance and user transparency.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: [Refund reason/notes] - For regulatory/contextual info. Documents why a refund is issued; atomic per event.

models.name: payment_audits
models.description:
[Payment/Discount/Transaction Audit Log] - Implements evidence chain, immutability, and compliance requirements from multiple specification points. This table tracks all changes (state, value, configuration) in payments, discounts, refunds, voucher activities, etc. No aggregated or calculated values are persisted; all logs are atomic, normalized events.

Each log entry references the affected entity (by type), time of event, actor (user/system). Provides audit, forensic, fraud mitigation and compliance trail.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique audit log entry.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Actor's {@link users.id}. Who performed this audit-tracked action; user or system account. Null for automated events but trackable for regulatory trace.

plainFields.name: entity_type
plainFields.description: [Entity type] - Implements polymorphic audit of payments, discounts, refunds, etc. Required for evidence/data tracking. For example: 'payment', 'discount', 'refund'.

plainFields.name: entity_id
plainFields.description: [Entity ID] - Target entity's primary key. Maintains atomicity. For example: references payments.id or discounts.id.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: [Action taken] - Logical action (e.g., 'create', 'update', 'apply', 'fail', 'refund') accomplished by this audit event. Required for end-to-end evidence chain. Maintains normalization.

plainFields.name: old_value
plainFields.description: [Previous state/value] - Optional snapshot for evidence. For example, payment status before update. Nullable for creates. Maintains normalization and evidence context.

plainFields.name: new_value
plainFields.description: [New state/value] - Resulting value or config. Nullable for deletes.

plainFields.name: timestamp
plainFields.description: [Audit event time] - Atomic/durable record of the precise event occurrence. Maintains 3NF, audit, and compliance requirements.

models.name: message_threads
models.description:
[Message Thread] - This implements the conversation thread grouping requirement from the 'Communication, Review & Sentiment Analysis' module. 

Groups together all related user-to-user or user-to-support messages into distinct threads, enabling clear organization and session-based conversation flows. Maintains 3NF by never storing derived or redundant message data—each thread keeps only identifying and stateful information. For example, a single thread can encompass multiple back-and-forth messages between a customer and support agent.

Key relationships: links to participants via foreign keys or through junction tables (future extension), referenced by messages and possibly notifications.
Special behaviors: Thread archival/deletion must preserve audit trails; never hard-delete for compliance.

foreignFields.name: created_by_user_id
foreignFields.description: Creator user's {@link users.id}.

plainFields.name: subject
plainFields.description:
[Thread subject] - Implements the requirement for thread labeling and discoverability.

Business meaning: Subject or title for top-level navigation, search, and summarization. Ensures normalization by separating core thread data from actual messages. Example: 'Order #1342 Support'.

plainFields.name: archived
plainFields.description: [Thread archival flag] - Implements requirement for evidence tracking and data preservation. Business meaning: Soft deletion/archival for audit purposes. Normalization: separate status flag, not affecting contained messages. Example: Thread archive action by user or admin.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Thread creation timestamp] - Implements audit/evidence requirement. Timestamp when thread was created. Normalization: atomic time, never duplicated from contained messages. Example: Show creation moment in thread list, regardless of message activity.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Thread last modified timestamp] - Implements recency for sorting/searching. Updated when participants act on the thread (send/receive message, archive, etc.). Normalization: always atomic, never copied or calculated from child message times. Example: Sort by latest update in UI.

models.name: messages
models.description:
[Message] - Implements the transactional communication entity requirement from the 'Communication, Review, and Sentiment Analysis' document. 

Represents individual messages (text, image, or system notification) exchanged within a message thread. Maintains strict 3NF—only atomic message and linkage data. For example, a customer question and a vendor response, with each message linked to user and thread.

Key relationships: references sender (user), target thread, and optionally parent message (for replies/quoting). 
Special behaviors: All changes are audited; messages are never deleted, only flagged. Attachments/media handled externally for evidence integrity.

foreignFields.name: thread_id
foreignFields.description: Thread's {@link message_threads.id} this message belongs to.

foreignFields.name: sender_user_id
foreignFields.description: Sender's {@link users.id}.

foreignFields.name: parent_message_id
foreignFields.description: Optional parent message's {@link messages.id} for reply/tree structure.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: [Message content] - Implements the raw message body/evidence tracking. Primary user/customer or system content. Never pre-calculated. Example: Support question, reply, or notification message.

plainFields.name: message_type
plainFields.description: [Message type] - Implements conversational workflow logic. Values include: 'user', 'system', 'notification', or custom types. Maintains normalization by storing type info atomically. Example: 'user' = human, 'system' = order status update, etc.

plainFields.name: sent_at
plainFields.description: [Send timestamp] - Time the message was dispatched. Maintains normalization by being atomic, always set on creation. Example: Populate message log or sort.

plainFields.name: read_at
plainFields.description: [Read timestamp] - Time the recipient viewed the message. Maintains normalization by being optional, never duplicated or inferred. Example: Unread badge logic.

plainFields.name: archived
plainFields.description: [Archived flag] - Strict evidence preservation, marking messages without deletion. Normalization compliance: atomic per message, not inherited from thread. Example: Hide from primary inbox but retained for audit.

models.name: notifications
models.description:
[Notification] - Implements the user notification system requirement as described under communication/event modules. 

Captures system-/event-driven notifications linked to users and, if relevant, threads or orders. Maintains 3NF by never duplicating event data from source entities; only logs atomic notification facts. Example: 'Order shipped', 'New message', or 'Sale started'.

Key relationships: references user, may link to thread or other context entity.
Special behaviors: Tracks read/unread status and delivery timestamp; old records never deleted for evidence.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Notified user's {@link users.id}.

foreignFields.name: thread_id
foreignFields.description: Related thread's {@link message_threads.id}, if any.

plainFields.name: notification_type
plainFields.description: [Type indicator] - Implements notification categorization; e.g., 'system', 'message', 'promotion'. Normalization: Single source of event type per notification. Example: Used for filtering in notification center.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: [Notification content] - Implements atomic event evidence; real message dispatched to user. Normalization: content held here, not duplicated from other entities. Example: 'Your order #1234 shipped'.

plainFields.name: sent_at
plainFields.description: [Notification dispatch time] - Time when delivered to user. Normalization: atomic per notification. Example: Sorting notifications, TTL enforcement.

plainFields.name: read_at
plainFields.description: [Notification read time] - When user viewed notification. Normalization: atomic, optional per record. Example: Mark as read upon open.

plainFields.name: archived
plainFields.description: [Archived flag] - Keeps notification for historical evidence. Never physically deleted. Example: Mute or archive by user action.

models.name: reviews
models.description:
[Review] - Implements product/service review entity from the 'Communication, Review & Sentiment Analysis' business module.

Represents authentic and versioned user-submitted reviews. Maintains strict 3NF: only atomic review attributes—content, media, metadata, never derived or aggregated. Example: User review for a purchased product, versioned for edit history.

Key relationships: References user, product/service, ties to moderation and sentiment logs.
Special behaviors: Supports multilingual data, evidence archiving, evidence-preserving versioning for edits and compliance.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Author user's {@link users.id}.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Reviewed product's {@link products.id}.

foreignFields.name: parent_review_id
foreignFields.description: Optional parent review's {@link reviews.id}, for reply/hierarchical structure.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: [Review content] - Main review body, implements the core business requirement for evidence-preserved user feedback. Normalization: only atomic text here. Example: User's product experience.

plainFields.name: language_code
plainFields.description: [Review language code] - Implements multicultural and accessibility requirement. Holds locale for review. Normalization: only atomic value, never derived. Example: 'en', 'ko', 'fr'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Review creation timestamp] - When submitted by user. Example: timeline displays, compliance logs.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Last modification time] - Latest edit, present on update. Example: show edit history.

plainFields.name: verified_purchase
plainFields.description: [Purchase verification flag] - Implements fraud prevention and authenticity. Set if review relates to verified purchase. Example: 'True' for eligible buyers only.

plainFields.name: archived
plainFields.description: [Archived flag] - Soft delete for audit and evidence. Never physically removed. Example: Admin-moderated reviews.

models.name: review_media
models.description:
[Review Media] - Implements the requirement to allow image/video attachments for reviews while enforcing normalization and evidence archiving.

References review, media asset, and stores metadata. Only atomic linkage and media attributes; evaluation or calculated fields in other tables only (e.g., media count in views). Example: Multiple images for a product review.

Key relationships: references review and an external media entity (for expansion). 
Special behaviors: Only links and descriptive attributes; media storage handled elsewhere.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: Linked review's {@link reviews.id}.

plainFields.name: media_type
plainFields.description: [Attachment type] - 'image', 'video', etc. Normalization: atomic classification. Example: Used for gallery, filter.

plainFields.name: uri
plainFields.description: [Media URI] - Directly links to storage asset. Maintains normalization by not duplicating data. Example: S3/GCS location or CDN path.

plainFields.name: alt_text
plainFields.description: [Alt text] - Accessibility and multicultural support. Describes image/video for a11y. Example: 'User photo of red sneakers'.

plainFields.name: sequence
plainFields.description: [Display sequence] - Implements ordered media logic. Maintains normalized integer, not inferred or derived. Example: Order of images as shown in UI.

models.name: review_moderations
models.description:
[Review Moderation] - Implements evidence-preserved moderation actions on reviews as required by compliance, fraud prevention, and audit modules. 

Stores atomic records of each moderation: action, moderator, decision, timestamp, rationale. Maintains strict normalization (no aggregation, no calculated fields). Example: Admin removes, restores, or flags a review for abusive content.

Key relationships: references moderated review and moderator user.
Special behaviors: All moderation events strictly immutable, producing an audit trail.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: Moderated review's {@link reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: moderator_user_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator user's {@link users.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: [Moderation action] - 'remove', 'restore', 'flag', etc. Required for audit. Example: Used as evidence on compliance review.

plainFields.name: rationale
plainFields.description: [Reason/rationale] - Explanation by moderator. Normalization: only atomic string. Example: Why review was removed/flagged.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Timestamp] - When moderation occurred. Normalized as atomic point in time. Example: Legal holds.

models.name: review_sentiments
models.description:
[Review Sentiment] - Implements versioned and AI-powered sentiment analysis for reviews as described in Sentiment Analysis requirements.

Captures analysis model/version, result, and timestamp for every processed review. Maintains strict normalization: no pre-calculated fields. Example: 'Positive/negative/neutral' per review version, tied to model run.

Key relationships: references review and AI model/version.
Special behaviors: Multiple entries allowed for model runs, with timestamped trail for evidence.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: Analyzed review's {@link reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: ai_model_version_id
foreignFields.description: AI model version's {@link ai_model_versions.id} used for analysis.

plainFields.name: sentiment
plainFields.description: [Sentiment result] - Implements the core outcome (e.g., 'positive', 'negative', 'neutral'). Atomic per analysis, never derived. Example: For dashboard reporting.

plainFields.name: score
plainFields.description: [Sentiment score] - Numeric value indicating polarity/confidence. Maintains normalization as atomic output. Example: Model's confidence in prediction.

plainFields.name: analyzed_at
plainFields.description: [Timestamp] - When sentiment analysis executed.

models.name: sentiment_analysis_logs
models.description:
[Sentiment Analysis Log] - Implements full evidence and model input/output preservation for every sentiment analysis run, fulfilling the tracking requirements set in advanced AI and compliance modules.

Stores all model input, output, AI version, and raw evidence for legal hold/audit. Maintains strict 3NF by holding only atomic data elements, never calculated or aggregate. Example: A record per sentiment inference, with trace of data and rationale.

Key relationships: references review, ai_model_version.
Special behaviors: Immutable, long-retained for compliance and model debugging.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: Analyzed review's {@link reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: ai_model_version_id
foreignFields.description: AI version's {@link ai_model_versions.id} used for sentiment.

plainFields.name: raw_input
plainFields.description: [Raw model input] - Stores original text or preprocessed structure input to model. Maintains normalization: atomic capture only. Example: JSON of features or string blob.

plainFields.name: output
plainFields.description: [Raw model output] - Full inference result, possibly JSON. Maintains normalization, not aggregated. Example: Model's output structure as-is for trace/debug.

plainFields.name: model_version
plainFields.description: [Model version string] - Redundant to FK for compliance readability. Maintains normalization: atomic version string. Example: 'v1.2.2-EN-SENTIMENT'.

plainFields.name: analyzed_at
plainFields.description: [Analysis timestamp] - When analysis was run. Maintains normalization as atomic timestamp. Example: Compliance audit.

models.name: favorites
models.description:
[Favorites Management Table] - This implements the favorite/bookmarking system as specified in section 07 of the requirements report.

Manages the user's bookmarks and favorite items, supporting evidence-based, auditable user preference tracking. Maintains 3NF by separating only the favorite relationship (user-content), leaving additional data (history, metadata, personalization) in related entities. For example, this table allows users to mark any product as a favorite and organizes the link between user and product for AI/analytics workflows.

Key relationships: Linked to {@link users.id}, {@link products.id}, with cascaded deletion on user or product removal.
Special behaviors: Immutable, evidence-preserving (soft-delete with audit via personalization_audit), composite uniqueness constraint to ensure a user cannot favorite the same product twice.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique favorite record identifier, complying with audit and evidence requirements.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description:
Belonged user's {@link users.id}.
Links the favorite action to the profile, supporting analytics, consent, and privacy compliance.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description:
Target product's {@link products.id}.
Points to the favorited product, supporting contextual personalization, product analytics, and AI recommendations.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for when the favorite record was created. Implements evidence preservation and auditing as required in the compliance sections. For example, enables reconstructing user preference timelines.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-deletion timestamp to maintain evidence preservation and non-repudiation. Null if active. For example, keeps an audit trail for regulatory requests.

models.name: bookmarks
models.description:
[Bookmark Table] - Implements user-defined bookmark/organization of products/content, as called for in the Favorites and Personalization requirements.

Acts as a refinement on the favorite concept, enabling organization and metadata for bookmarks. Maintains normalization (3NF) by linking only user and product, and keeping additional metadata (e.g. category/folder/tag) here, rather than the core favorite link. For example, a user can tag or categorize favorites using bookmarks.

Key relationships: Linked to {@link users.id} and {@link products.id}; supports bidirectional linkage for advanced queries and analytics.
Special behaviors: Composite uniqueness constraint for per-user bookmarks; supports optional custom_folder for personalized organization.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description:
Belonged user's {@link users.id}.
Supports permission checks, analytics, and data retrieval.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description:
Referenced product's {@link products.id}.
Pinpoints the bookmarked product for analysis and retrieval.

plainFields.name: custom_folder
plainFields.description: Optional organizational label or folder for this bookmark. Implements user segmentation for evidence and personalization. For example, user groups bookmarks under "Wish List".

plainFields.name: tag
plainFields.description: Optional user-defined tag for the bookmark for enhanced organization and analytics. Maintains normalization and is kept atomic. For example: "Winter Sale".

plainFields.name: note
plainFields.description: Optional user note attached to the bookmark, evidence for personalization. For example, "Gift idea for Mom."

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for bookmark creation, audit and personalization evidence compliance.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Optional timestamp for soft deletion (audit/evidence preservation requirement).

models.name: personalization_events
models.description:
[Personalization Event Table] - Implements tracking of all personalization actions/events impacting user experience, specified in section 07 and 08 (AI & Data Operations).

Captures evidence and metadata for when a user receives, reacts to, or interacts with a personalized recommendation. Maintains 3NF by relegating feature data and detailed analytics logs to other tables. For example, this enables tracing which recommendation was shown, clicked, or dismissed.

Key relationships: Linked to {@link users.id}, {@link recommendations.id}, {@link products.id}. Supports AI model tracking.
Special behaviors: Immutable event log for audit/compliance, supports detailed event-type taxonomy via 'event_type'.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique record for a personalization event.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged user's {@link users.id}. Links event to user profile for analytics and personalization history.

foreignFields.name: recommendation_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged recommendation's {@link recommendations.id}. Reference to the suggestion served in this event.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Target product's {@link products.id}. The product associated with the event, for traceability and feedback learning.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Type of personalization event (e.g., view, click, save, dismiss). Enables advanced analytics and model explainability. Normalized—categorical and atomic. For example: 'RECOMMENDATION_SERVED'.

plainFields.name: model_version
plainFields.description: AI/ML model version used in generating the recommendation; implements explainability and regulatory compliance requirements.

plainFields.name: context
plainFields.description: Optional context information for event (device, locale, etc.). Captures multi-channel/locale evidence as per requirements.

plainFields.name: timestamp
plainFields.description: Timestamp for when personalization event occurred. Implements evidence and audit traceability.

models.name: recommendations
models.description:
[Recommendation Table] - Implements the storage of AI/ML-driven recommendation deliveries as required for personalization, evidence tracking, and explainability (requirements sections 07 & 08).

Each record links a recommendation to a user and a product at a specific time, tracks which model/version served it, and whether the result was seen or acted upon. Maintains normalization by not pre-calculating favorites or analytics.

Key relationships: References {@link users.id} (who received), {@link products.id} (recommended content), and links to personalization events.
Special behaviors: Composite uniqueness for user, product, and timestamp (cannot re-recommend exact same thing at the same time), GIN index for rationale explainability/search.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged user's {@link users.id}. User receiving the recommendation.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Target product's {@link products.id}. Product being recommended.

plainFields.name: model_id
plainFields.description: AI model identifier generating the recommendation; for compliance and retrain audit.

plainFields.name: model_version
plainFields.description: AI/ML model version generating this recommendation. Required for audit and transparency (regulatory).

plainFields.name: rationale
plainFields.description: Optional human/machine-readable rationale, used for explainability and audit trail per compliance needs.

plainFields.name: recommendation_time
plainFields.description: Timestamp when recommendation was delivered. Required for continuous feedback/monitoring.

models.name: personalization_audits
models.description:
[Personalization Audit Table] - Implements the evidence-preserving audit log for all personalization and favorite-related actions, as required for regulatory, explainability, and continuous improvement needs (sections 07, 08, 09). 

Stores non-repudiable, immutable evidence for sensitive user actions related to favorites, bookmarks, recommendations, and AI-triggered changes. Maintains full normalization by referencing all participating entities and ensuring no pre-calculated or derived fields.

Key relationships: References {@link users.id}, {@link favorites.id}, {@link bookmarks.id}, {@link recommendations.id}, {@link personalization_events.id}. Cross-links actions for holistic compliance and model improvement.
Special behaviors: Write-once (append-only), cryptographically signed evidence, all fields atomic.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged user's {@link users.id}. Links the personalization action to specific user.

foreignFields.name: favorite_id
foreignFields.description: Optional reference to {@link favorites.id}, maintained for evidence and retroactive compliance.

foreignFields.name: bookmark_id
foreignFields.description: Optional reference to {@link bookmarks.id}, maintained for evidence and retroactive compliance.

foreignFields.name: recommendation_id
foreignFields.description: Optional reference to {@link recommendations.id}, to track audit events involving recommendations.

foreignFields.name: personalization_event_id
foreignFields.description: Optional link to {@link personalization_events.id}, audit evidence for anything with contextual event.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type/category of the audit event (e.g. ADD_FAVORITE, REMOVE_BOOKMARK, SERVE_RECOMMENDATION). Normalized/atomic for querying/compliance. For example: 'ACTIONS'.

plainFields.name: evidence_hash
plainFields.description: Cryptographic hash of the action/event for non-repudiation, as required for compliance.

plainFields.name: timestamp
plainFields.description: Exact time of audit event for regulatory trace/compliance; enables reconstructing chain-of-custody.

models.name: ai_models
models.description:
AI Model Registry - This implements the requirement for a unified model registry and governance from section 08 (Advanced AI and Data Operations) of the requirements. 

Central repository for all AI/ML models used within the system, holding business metadata (name, description, model type, owner), categorization, and audit fields to enforce model governance, version tracking, and compliance. Maintains 3NF by not duplicating version, deployment, or decision info. For example, registering recommendation, dynamic pricing, or sentiment models. 

Key relationships: Connects with {@link ai_model_versions} for actual model instances, links to organizations and users for ownership, supports audit evidence. 
Special behaviors: Uniqueness constraint on (name, organization), all business fields are atomic and normalized.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key - Unique identifier for each AI model.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: Owning organization's {@link organizations.id} - Implements multidomain model governance requirement. Organization context for model accountability.

foreignFields.name: owner_id
foreignFields.description: Owning user's {@link users.id} - Maintains audit trace and role-based model management.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Model name - Implements model identification aspect. Human-friendly, unique per organization. Prevents duplication, maintains normalization. Example: 'prod-recommendation-2024'

plainFields.name: model_type
plainFields.description: Model type - Implements model taxonomy. Business meaning: e.g., recommendation, pricing, fraud. Ensures model classification is atomic. Example: 'recommendation'

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Description - Human-intelligible summary, implements evidence/traceability requirement. For example: 'Collaborative filtering model for top sellers'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp - When model metadata was first registered. Atomic, not derived.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Update timestamp - When model metadata was last changed. Ensures normalization. Example: model taxonomy change.

models.name: ai_model_versions
models.description:
AI Model Versioning - Implements the requirement for full model lifecycle tracking and explainability from section 08 (Advanced AI and Data Operations) requirement.

Stores concrete versioned instances for each AI model, supporting lineage and deployment traceability. Complies with 3NF by never embedding decision or request data, only atomic version metadata. For example, each trained model artifact, versioned and ready for deployment or audit. 

Key relationships: Foreign key to {@link ai_models}, holds deployment metadata. Special behaviors: Unique constraint on (ai_model_id, version_hash).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key - Unique identifier for each model version.

foreignFields.name: ai_model_id
foreignFields.description: Parent model's {@link ai_models.id} - Traces version lineage. Enforces normalization: no model metadata duplication.

plainFields.name: version
plainFields.description: Version string - Implements versioning policy. e.g., 'v1.4.3', ensures atomicity, never derived. For tracking deployments.

plainFields.name: version_hash
plainFields.description: Version hash - Immutable hash of model artifact, supporting evidence preservation and integrity verification. For compliance (e.g. audit trails).

plainFields.name: artifact_url
plainFields.description: Artifact URI - Location of the model artifact in secure storage. Ensures normalization by referencing only, not storing contents.

plainFields.name: framework
plainFields.description: ML framework - Business context: e.g., 'TensorFlow', 'PyTorch'. Maintains atomic, normalized record of build platform.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: Version metadata - Implements evidence trace. JSON or key-value string for atomic version-specific fields (hyperparameters, notes). Never derived.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp - Atomic, when this version was created.

plainFields.name: deployed_at
plainFields.description: Deployment timestamp - When this model version was deployed (if ever). Null if never deployed. Atomic. For regulatory/audit evidence.

models.name: ai_training_data
models.description:
AI Training Data Registry - Implements mandatory dataset tracking requirement from Advanced AI and Data Operations section.

Catalogs all datasets—internal or external—used in AI/ML training runs. Business purpose: ensuring evidence preservation, model governance, and regulatory compliance. 3NF maintained: no embedding feature or decision data, only atomic dataset metadata. For example, registering user purchase logs, product metadata, reviews, or imported partners' data feeds as AI input.

Key relationships: Models dataset-to-model and version relationships, supports traceability. Special behaviors: Uniqueness constraint on (name, version, source_uri).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key - Unique identifier for training dataset.

foreignFields.name: ai_model_id
foreignFields.description: Associated model's {@link ai_models.id} - Optional, as datasets may predate or span multiple models. Maintains traceable, normalized context.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Dataset name - Human-friendly identifier, e.g., '2024Q1-purchases'. Required. Normalization via uniqueness constraint with version+uri.

plainFields.name: version
plainFields.description: Dataset version - e.g., 'v1', '202404', for traceability and reproducibility. Implements evidence requirement. Required.

plainFields.name: source_uri
plainFields.description: Source URI - Link to immutable, secured dataset in storage. Ensures data separation, not duplication. Required.

plainFields.name: schema_hash
plainFields.description: Schema hash - Hash of dataset schema, for evidence and change detection. Ensures atomicity, never derived.

plainFields.name: record_count
plainFields.description: Record count - Number of records/rows in the dataset. Atomic, reported only. Example: 10000000 (for 10M sale records).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp - When dataset was first registered.

models.name: ai_feature_store
models.description:
AI Feature Store Registry - Implements the centralized feature tracking and evidence preservation requirement from the Advanced AI and Data Operations section.

Native registry for feature sets engineered for AI model training and inference. 3NF is ensured: field-level definitions of each feature set, no denormalization or pre-calculation. For example, storing user-product interaction feature set names, their schema description, and originating training dataset.

Key relationships: Links to {@link ai_training_data} (origin of features) and {@link ai_model_versions} (using version). Special behaviors: Uniqueness constraint on (ai_model_version_id, name).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key - Unique identifier for a feature set.

foreignFields.name: ai_model_version_id
foreignFields.description: Target model version's {@link ai_model_versions.id} - Implements model lineage traceability requirement. Required.

foreignFields.name: ai_training_data_id
foreignFields.description: Source dataset's {@link ai_training_data.id} - Evidence link for feature extraction. Nullable, not all features require direct linkage. Maintains normalization.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Feature set name - Human-friendly label, e.g. 'user-purchase-matrix-v1'. Normalized and unique per model version. Example: 'sentiment-review-set-202404'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Description - Detailed documentation for audit/compliance. Evidence trace for explainability. Example: 'Features for collaborative filtering.'

plainFields.name: schema
plainFields.description: Feature schema - Machine-readable JSON schema representing the feature set structure. Maintains normalization; no denormalized data here.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp - Evidence of when engineering completed.

models.name: ai_decision_logs
models.description:
AI Decision Log - Implements mandatory logging and explainability requirement from Advanced AI and Data Operations section.

Immutable, atomic record of each automated decision or inference by any AI model. Business purpose: evidence for compliance (GDPR 'right to explanation'), debugging, monitoring, and model improvement. Keeps schema atomic: never stores denormalized or summarized results, only per-decision facts and links. For example, logging a recommendation output for a specific user or order.

Key relationships: References {@link ai_model_version}, target entity (user, product, order, etc.), audit details. Special behaviors: Enforces data provenance via foreign keys and immutable timestamps.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key - Unique identifier for a decision log.

foreignFields.name: ai_model_version_id
foreignFields.description: Associated model version's {@link ai_model_versions.id} - Tracks which version produced this decision. Required.

foreignFields.name: target_user_id
foreignFields.description: Target user's {@link users.id} - The user affected by decision. Nullable where not user-specific. Maintains normalization, never derived.

plainFields.name: target_entity
plainFields.description: Target entity - Implements audit tracking of affected object. E.g., 'order', 'product', 'review'. Prevents denormalization by not embedding entity fields.

plainFields.name: target_entity_id
plainFields.description: Target entity ID - The ID of the affected object (atomic, never joined/duplicated), e.g. product or order ID. Maintains strict normalization.

plainFields.name: decision
plainFields.description: Decision outcome - E.g., 'recommend', 'block', 'price=12.50'. Business context: ensures traceability, atomicity, never computed. For model explainability.

plainFields.name: input_snapshot
plainFields.description: Input snapshot - JSON or base64 blob representing the exact input to the AI at inference, for audit and debugging. 3NF: atomic per event.

plainFields.name: rationale
plainFields.description: Model rationale - Explanation for the decision, if available. Supports compliance, 3NF, and human override/audit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of decision event for audit/evidence.

models.name: ai_feedback
models.description:
AI Feedback Log - Implements feedback loop requirement for continuous learning and audit from Advanced AI and Data Operations section.

Stores explicit and implicit feedback for each AI decision event, connecting user actions or operator overrides to the original model inference. Enables automated model retraining, human override validation, and explainability for regulators. 3NF strict: each field atomic, all links explicit, no denormalization.

Key relationships: Links {@link ai_decision_logs} (original decision), user, and model version. Special behaviors: Composite index on (decision_log_id, user_id, feedback_type).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key - Unique identifier for feedback event.

foreignFields.name: decision_log_id
foreignFields.description: Original decision log's {@link ai_decision_logs.id} - Implements feedback-data linkage for model retraining. Required.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: User's {@link users.id} submitting feedback or being observed for implicit signals. Allows anonymous/null for auto signals.

plainFields.name: feedback_type
plainFields.description: Type of feedback - E.g., 'accepted', 'dismissed', 'overridden', 'implicit-click'. Atomic per event. Implements feedback/data tracking requirement.

plainFields.name: feedback_value
plainFields.description: Feedback value - E.g., 'positive', 'negative', 'rating=5'. Business context: for retraining, analysis. Strictly atomic, not computed.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: Metadata - (Optional) JSON/string with UI context, device info, or feedback rationale. Atomic/non-derived, supports explainability.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of feedback event. Maintains evidence, not derived.

models.name: security_event
models.description:
Security Event Logging - This implements event logging and evidence preservation for all security-relevant actions as per Section 2 (Critical Data Auditing) and Section 4 (Data Integrity & Preservation) of the requirements. 

Records all system-level security-related occurrences, capturing actor, context, and timestamp for each. Maintains 3NF by storing only atomic event-level data and referencing origin entities via foreign keys. For example, an API token rotation, a failed login attempt, or privilege escalation. Key relationships: links to relevant user, session, and API client where applicable. Special behaviors: immutable; no deletion, supports audit retrieval.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each security event record.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to initiating user's {@link users.id}. If system-initiated, can be null. Ensures mapping of event context to user for audit.

foreignFields.name: session_id
foreignFields.description: Associated session {@link sessions.id}. Links actions to active session for traceability.

foreignFields.name: api_client_id
foreignFields.description: API client context {@link api_clients.id} under which the event occurred, if relevant.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Category of security event (e.g., 'login_attempt', 'token_rotation', 'permission_update') - Implements Section 2 (Critical Data Auditing). Encodes nature of event for context-rich evidence. For example, used for analytics and compliance dashboards. Required.

plainFields.name: event_details
plainFields.description: Human- and machine-readable details of the event - Implements evidence preservation requirement. Provides business context; can include affected fields, prior values, or policy triggers. For example, stores JSON stringified details. Required.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp of the event record - Ensures non-repudiation as required for audit trails and regulatory compliance.

models.name: permission
models.description:
Permission Registry - This implements dynamic and fine-grained permission tracking aligned to Section 3 (Access Control & Permission). 

Tracks all permissions available in the platform, with atomic records for each permission entity. 3NF maintained: only basic attributes and references to associated policy. For example, permissions like 'order.edit', 'discount.apply'. Key relationships: can be referenced in policy and role mappings. Special behaviors: unique codes enforced, never deleted (for historical policy linkage).
