primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for permission.

foreignFields.name: policy_id
foreignFields.description: Associated policy's {@link policy.id}. Connects permission entity to rules and conditions applying to it.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Unique permission code (e.g., 'user.read', 'order.cancel') - Implements fine-grained access control as required by Section 3. For example, used in runtime permission checks. Must be unique across system. Required.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of what the permission entails - Maps to regulatory and explainability requirements. For example, describes business context for UI and audit tools. Required.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of permission creation - For audit and evidence preservation as per requirements.

models.name: policy
models.description:
Permission Policy - This model implements Section 3 and 5 (dynamic policy-driven permission enforcement, regulatory compliance tracking). 

Represents a logical grouping of permissions with optional conditions or constraints. Maintains 3NF by storing only atomic policy-level data. For example, policies for 'admin_only', time-bound permissions, region-limited access. Key relationships: can be referenced by permissions, roles, or external API modules. Special behaviors: policies remain after deletion for legal traceability.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for a policy.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Human-readable policy name - Implements requirement for business logic explainability and traceability. For example, 'Admin Global', 'EU Data Export'. Required.

plainFields.name: conditions
plainFields.description: Serialized JSON or code describing policy constraints/logic - Aligns with dynamic enforcement and compliance. For example, specifies conditions such as 'only during office hours'. Required.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp for policy record - Provides evidence trail needed for audits. Required.

models.name: audit_log
models.description:
System Audit Log - Implements end-to-end non-repudiable logging for all system and user actions, in accordance with Section 4 and 5 (Data Integrity, Evidence, Audit-Ready Structure). 

Stores immutable audit records for every critical operation and event. 3NF achieved by isolating raw events with user, entity, and context references. Used for regulatory export, legal inquiry, and breach forensics. Key relationships: links to user, affected entity (as foreign key where possible), evidence_archive. Special behaviors: append-only; deletion prohibited.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique audit log record identifier.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: User actor responsible for action {@link users.id}. Enables user-centric audit filtering for compliance exports.

foreignFields.name: evidence_archive_id
foreignFields.description: Archived evidence snapshot {@link evidence_archive.id} associated with event.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: Type of action performed (e.g., 'create', 'update', 'delete', 'payment.approve') - Implements requirement for business trace and explainability. For example, facilitates compliance dashboard queries. Required.

plainFields.name: entity_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity affected (e.g., 'order', 'user', 'review') - Enables entity-level filtering and integrity checks. Required.

plainFields.name: entity_id
plainFields.description: ID of the affected entity instance - Ensures traceability down to individual records, fulfilling audit trail requirements. Nullable for system events not targeting specific entity.

plainFields.name: context
plainFields.description: JSON-encoded metadata/context of the audit event - Supports regulatory and forensics use. For example, before/after data, machine/environmental context. Required.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of audit log creation - For evidence and compliance enforcement. Required.

models.name: compliance_report
models.description:
Compliance Report - This table fulfills Section 5 requirements for regulatory export, oversight, and drilldown on AI-driven or security events. 

Stores generated compliance reports (GDPR, CCPA, internal regs) and their metadata. Maintains 3NF by only referencing report owner/user, storing atomic report attributes. For example, a GDPR export delivered to a user, or a monthly payment compliance summary. Key relationships: owners (user, organization), linked evidence. Special behaviors: cannot be edited once published, may be superseded by later reports.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique compliance report identifier.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Owner or data subject {@link users.id} for individual reports.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: Owning organization {@link organizations.id}, if applicable.

plainFields.name: report_type
plainFields.description: Classification of compliance report (e.g., 'GDPR_EXPORT', 'CCPA_AUDIT') - Implements export and oversight requirements. Required.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Status of report (e.g., 'pending', 'published', 'superseded') - Ensures auditability of report progression. For example, status visible in admin dashboards. Required.

plainFields.name: generated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when report was generated - For audit and tracking as per requirements. Required.

plainFields.name: published_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when report was published/delivered; required for evidence trail and deadline compliance. Nullable if not yet published.

models.name: data_retention
models.description:
Data Retention Policy - This implements configurable data retention, deletion, and legal hold logic (Section 5), supporting entity-level configurations and traceability.

Stores data retention policy per data subject or entity. 3NF maintained by separating atomic policy settings per record. For example, policies for user data, payment log, or review. Key relationships: can be linked to entity, organization, user for context. Special behaviors: enforced by backend logic, referenced by compliance_report, deletion must leave audit trace.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for data_retention policy record.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: Organization to which retention policy applies {@link organizations.id}. Enables B2B use cases and regulatory separation.

plainFields.name: entity_type
plainFields.description: Entity data type subject to retention policy (e.g., 'user', 'order', 'review') - Aligns with regulatory entity-level retention needs. Required.

plainFields.name: retention_period_days
plainFields.description: Retention period in days (e.g., 365, 1095) - Ensures compliance with regulatory and contract requirements. For example, controls automated deletion logic. Required.

plainFields.name: is_legal_hold
plainFields.description: Legal hold status - Implements requirement for holding deletion in progress during litigation/audit. For example, backend logic enforces this. Required.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Policy record creation time - Fulfills requirement for audit trail per policy change. Required.

models.name: evidence_archive
models.description:
Evidence Archive - Implements immutable, compressed archiving for critical evidence as required in Section 4 (Evidence Preservation) and Section 5 (Compliance). 

Stores compressed or signed evidence payloads for system operations, enabling legal, forensics, and audit exports. 3NF enforced by separating blob storage and atomic references. For example, a zipped export of user data provided for GDPR DSAR; a signed PDF of payment logs. Key relationships: referenced in audit_log, compliance_report, and other tables where evidence may be required. Special behaviors: blob/blob reference is immutable and append-only; cannot be deleted, only superseded.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique evidence archive record identifier.

plainFields.name: evidence_type
plainFields.description: Type/category of archived evidence (e.g., 'GDPR_DSAR_EXPORT', 'PAYMENT_LOG_SNAPSHOT') - Fulfilling evidence preservation and compliance needs. Required.

plainFields.name: blob_url
plainFields.description: URI for archived evidence binary/payload - Implements requirement for logical separation of data and reference. For example, S3/GCS/Blob Storage link. Required.

plainFields.name: size_bytes
plainFields.description: Size of the archived evidence in bytes - For audit, integrity, and storage cost assessment. Fulfills traceability requirements. Required.

plainFields.name: checksum
plainFields.description: Cryptographic hash (e.g., SHA256) for the stored evidence - Implements data integrity and non-repudiation patterns. Required.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of evidence creation/archival. Supports evidence chain enforcement. Required.

models.name: api_clients
models.description:
[API Client Registry] - This implements the client registration and management requirement for API and omnichannel extensibility from the scalability and integration section of the requirements. 

Business explanation: Represents all third-party, partner, or internal software clients authorized to interact with the platform via APIs or omnichannel connectors. Maintains 3NF compliance by only storing atomic client metadata and security configuration, with all usage/interaction history managed in separate audit/sessions models. For example, a registered ERP partner system or mobile app client would have an instance here.

Key relationships: Connected to API tokens (for issued secrets), audit logs (for operations), and integration channels (for channel associations).
Special behaviors: Certificate/public-key fields, client revocation and expiration, and strict uniqueness on client_name.

plainFields.name: client_name
plainFields.description:
[Client Name] - Implements the requirement for unique human-readable identification of the API/omnichannel client. 

Used for admin UI and logging, not as technical credential. Ensures normalization by separating identity from secrets. Example: 'Acme ERP Gateway'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
[Description] - Brief business description of client/app integration. 

For admins, auditability, and risk/compliance review. Atomic string for documentation. Example: 'Official mobile application for end-users.'

plainFields.name: contact_email
plainFields.description:
[Contact Email] - Administrative contact for support/issues. 

Used for notifications, incident response. Not a user reference. Atomic and unique per client. Example: 'devops@partner.com'.

plainFields.name: public_key
plainFields.description:
[Public Key or Certificate] - Implements the API client verification requirement for secure request signing, especially for B2B/integrated clients. 

Stored as text blob. No duplication or relational data. Example: PEM key/certificate.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description:
[Activation Status] - Is this API client currently permitted to call APIs/integrations? 

Implements the enable/disable for operational security and access controls. Not derived, not transitive. Example: Initially true upon onboarding.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
[Creation Timestamp] - When this client entry was registered. 

Evidence for audit, onboarding, and rotation policies. Atomic timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
[Revocation (Soft Delete) Timestamp] - When this client integration was revoked, decommissioned, or scheduled for archival. 

Evidence for audit/forensics. Soft delete pattern.

models.name: api_tokens
models.description:
[API Access Token] - This implements the secure API authentication/authorization requirement, tracking all issued credentials for API and integration client access, mapped to requirements for token lifecycle management and security event monitoring. 

Business explanation: Stores all tokens/secrets granted to a specific API client. Maintains 3NF: token value, issued scope, and expiry are atomic, with usage logs and audit in secondary tables. For example, an OAuth2/JWT token for Acme's integration client. 

Key relationships: Linked to api_clients, with cascaded deletion/invalidation support. 
Special behaviors: Token revocation, rotation, scope definition, expiry, and linkage to session and audit models.

foreignFields.name: api_client_id
foreignFields.description:
[API Client Reference] - Belonged API client's {@link api_clients.id}. 

Links the token to its registered client application for evidence and access validation.

plainFields.name: token_value
plainFields.description:
[Token Value] - Implements requirement to securely store issued access token (hashed/encrypted). 

Atomic (not derived), never duplicated in plain text. Example: Hashed OAuth2 JWT or custom token.

plainFields.name: scope
plainFields.description:
[Token Scope] - Business/technical permission associated with this token. 

Stored as delimited/structured string for 3NF. Example: 'read:orders,write:catalog'.

plainFields.name: issued_at
plainFields.description:
[Token Issued At] - Timestamp of when the token was created/granted. 

Strict evidence and compliance requirement.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description:
[Token Expiry] - When this access credential will expire, per business security/compliance rules. 

Atomic timestamp value. For example, 7 days from issue.

plainFields.name: revoked_at
plainFields.description:
[Token Revocation Timestamp] - If/when this token was manually invalidated, for incident response or admin action. 

Soft delete pattern, atomic value.

models.name: api_audits
models.description:
[API Audit Trail] - Implements the requirement for comprehensive evidence logging and traceability of all API/omnichannel activity for compliance, security, forensics, and analytics. 

Business explanation: Stores each API request/event record, including actor, endpoint, action, decision logic, input/output hashes and outcomes. Strictly normalized: each row is atomic, no aggregates or summaries. Used to reconstruct incident timelines, regulatory reviews, or AI feedback for model retraining. For example, logging a PATCH to order status API or a failed webhook delivery. 

Key relationships: Linked to api_clients, api_tokens, and integration_channels (omnichannel source). 
Special behaviors: No deletion; retention policy and evidence archiving instead.

foreignFields.name: api_client_id
foreignFields.description:
[API Client Reference] - Belonged API client from {@link api_clients.id}. 

Source of the request/session/event.

foreignFields.name: api_token_id
foreignFields.description:
[API Token Reference] - Credential used for this operation, {@link api_tokens.id}. 

Enables evidence mapping, forensics, and access validation.

foreignFields.name: integration_channel_id
foreignFields.description:
[Integration Channel Reference] - Omnichannel source of request/event {@link integration_channels.id}. 

E.g., 'web', 'mobileapp', 'partner_erp'.

plainFields.name: endpoint
plainFields.description:
[API Endpoint Path] - Implements requirement for full request path traceability. 

Atomic path string, e.g. '/v2/order/{id}/update'.

plainFields.name: http_method
plainFields.description:
[HTTP Method] - Captures action type for compliance ('GET', 'POST', etc.). 

Atomic, not derived. Example: 'POST'.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description:
[Actor/Subject ID] - UUID of user/service/entity causing action. 

Atomic reference. May reference user, partner, or system actor.

plainFields.name: decision_log_id
plainFields.description:
[AI Decision Log Reference] - If this API operation involved an automated/AI-based decision, reference unique log id. 

Supports explainability, model audit. May be nullable for non-AI flows.

plainFields.name: request_hash
plainFields.description:
[Request Body Hash] - Deterministic hash of input payload for integrity/evidence preservation. 

Prevents tampering. Atomic value, e.g. sha256(data).

plainFields.name: response_hash
plainFields.description:
[Response Body Hash] - Deterministic hash of returned payload for end-to-end evidence/auditing. 

Anti-tampering.

plainFields.name: is_success
plainFields.description:
[Success Flag] - Was this operation permitted/executed? 

For real-world forensics/audit, not derived. Atomic.

plainFields.name: status_code
plainFields.description:
[HTTP Status Code] - Final status from this request. 

Atomic integer. Example: 200, 401, 500.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
[Request Timestamp] - Time request was received and logged. 

Atomic timestamp for compliance and audit.

models.name: integration_channels
models.description:
[Integration Channel] - Implements the requirement to support omnichannel sources/connections and API gateways from the scalability and extensibility module. 

Business explanation: Each record represents an authorized source channel (e.g., web, mobile, external ERP, partner API gateway) that can initiate or receive events/integrations. Maintains 3NF and normalization: does not duplicate client/channel config, but links to associated sessions, audits, and webhooks. For example, a 'Point-of-Sale Kiosk' integration or a 'Partner CRM'. 

Key relationships: Referenced by channel_sessions, audits, and used for system events/analytics.

plainFields.name: channel_code
plainFields.description:
[Channel Code] - Unique technical identifier for the source/integration channel. 

Required for business logic, routing, and automation. Example: 'mobileapp', 'partner_erp'.

plainFields.name: channel_name
plainFields.description:
[Channel Name] - Human readable, unique/channel-scoped label for easier management. 

Not a code/slug. Example: 'Main Web Storefront'.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description:
[Activation Status] - Indicates if the channel is currently enabled for communication and integrations. 

Atomic, not derived. For compliance and automation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
[Registration Timestamp] - Channel setup/registration time for system auditability. 

Atomic timestamp. For evidence and analytics.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
[Deactivation (Soft Delete) Timestamp] - When this integration was formally ended (for audit/compliance). 

Implements soft delete pattern. Atomic timestamp.

models.name: channel_sessions
models.description:
[Channel Session/Instance] - Implements omnichannel session/lifecycle evidence for concurrent usage, device mapping, and scalability analysis, mapped to the requirement for cross-channel tracking and analytics. 

Business explanation: Each row represents a single connection period/session for a user/client/channel combination (e.g., a POS login, or mobile session). Restricts attributes to atomic values—expirations, tokens, associated references. For example, a customer on the web channel, switching to mobile with the same cart/order context.

Key relationships: Linked to integration_channels, api_tokens, and used for session state analytics.
Special behaviors: Session expiration/invalidations. All denormalized summaries go to mv_ tables only.

foreignFields.name: integration_channel_id
foreignFields.description:
[Integration Channel Reference] - Channel for this session, {@link integration_channels.id}. 

Atomic; no duplicates.

foreignFields.name: api_token_id
foreignFields.description:
[API Token Reference] - Access token that initiated this session {@link api_tokens.id}. 

Atomic; session always requires a token.

plainFields.name: user_id
plainFields.description:
[User Reference] - Optional user UUID linked to this session. 

When present, identifies the direct user; otherwise, may be system/integration. Example: buyer channel login, or anonymous device.

plainFields.name: session_key
plainFields.description:
[Session Key] - System-generated, opaque identifier for this channel session instance. 

Atomic string, for referencing in logs or context-passing APIs.

plainFields.name: started_at
plainFields.description:
[Started At Timestamp] - When this channel session began. 

Exact audit evidence, for compliance and automation.

plainFields.name: ended_at
plainFields.description:
[Ended At Timestamp] - When session was terminated (timeout, logout). 

Not derived. Null if still open.

models.name: webhook_events
models.description:
[Webhook Event/Notification] - Implements the external/internal event delivery and audit requirements for extensible integration, system notification, and partner automation. 

Business explanation: Captures each system or API-originated webhook event, including delivery state and evidence for retries/audits. Fully normalized—relationship to originating channel, destination, and technical params only (payloads not stored here, only hashes/IDs). For example, a notification to a partner when an order is updated, or price changes via API. 

Key relationships: Linked to integration_channels. Used for compliance, analytics, and incident response.
Special behaviors: Delivery tracking, retry evidence, event outcome codification, no denormalization (all summaries are in mv_ tables only).

foreignFields.name: integration_channel_id
foreignFields.description:
[Integration Channel Reference] - Channel that originated/scheduled the webhook {@link integration_channels.id}. 

Atomic for audit, routing, compliance.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description:
[Event Type] - Business/technical event code (e.g., 'order.updated', 'payment.completed'). 

Atomic, not derived. For routing and compliance purposes.

plainFields.name: destination_url
plainFields.description:
[Destination URL] - Target endpoint for webhook delivery. 

Atomic and unique per webhook. Never duplicated. Example: 'https://partner.com/hook'.

plainFields.name: attempt_count
plainFields.description:
[Attempt Count] - Number of delivery attempts made to destination. 

Atomic for evidence/audit. For example, incremented on retry.

plainFields.name: last_attempted_at
plainFields.description:
[Last Attempted Timestamp] - When a delivery was last tried. 

Atomic value for audit/troubleshooting.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description:
[Delivery Success Timestamp] - When webhook was successfully delivered. 

Audit log reference. Null if not completed.

plainFields.name: delivery_status
plainFields.description:
[Latest Delivery Status] - Code indicating delivery result ('pending','success','failed'). 

Atomic string, for system logic and evidence.

plainFields.name: event_hash
plainFields.description:
[Event Payload Hash] - Hashed identifier of request event, for evidence preservation and audit. 

Atomic and unique for event+payload. Example: sha256 of JSON/Payload.

 * Client

import * as runtime from './runtime/library.js';
import $Types = runtime.Types // general types
import $Public = runtime.Types.Public
import $Utils = runtime.Types.Utils
import $Extensions = runtime.Types.Extensions
import $Result = runtime.Types.Result

export type PrismaPromise<T> = $Public.PrismaPromise<T>


/**
 * Model users
 * [User Account Entity] - This implements the secure, scalable, privacy-first user management requirement from the User & Identity Management module. 
 * 
 * Provides foundational identities for the platform. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating identity from profile, session, and permissions. For example, links to user events, access logs, consents, and profiles. 
 * 
 * Key relationships: user_profiles, sessions, consents, access_logs, roles, organizations.
 * Special behaviors: usernames/emails are unique, secure credential storage, full traceability and audit logging.
 * 
 * @namespace Core
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type users = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$usersPayload>
/**
 * Model user_profiles
 * [User Profile Entity] - This implements the extended user attributes and multicultural/accessibility requirements. 
 * 
 * Contains personal information, preferences, localization, and accessibility settings, attached 1:1 to a user. Maintains 3NF by separating profile from credential and account data. Example: stores names, avatars, language, timezone, accessibility options. 
 * 
 * Key relationships: users (required), locales (optional).
 * Special behaviors: Only one profile per user, enforces privacy segregation from authentication data.
 * 
 * @namespace Core
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type user_profiles = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$user_profilesPayload>
/**
 * Model organizations
 * [Organization Entity] - This implements the multi-tenancy and B2B compliance requirement. 
 * 
 * Represents a logical business or retailer, to whom users, roles, resources may belong. Maintains 3NF: organization details are not repeated elsewhere. Supports future expansion for B2B, partner, and omnichannel flows. 
 * 
 * Key relationships: users, roles. 
 * Special behaviors: names/codes are unique within system.
 * 
 * @namespace Core
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type organizations = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$organizationsPayload>
/**
 * Model roles
 * [Role Entity] - Implements RBAC requirement for user access and multi-tenant permissioning. 3NF by separating roles from users. 
 * 
 * Defines named permission sets assignable to users (e.g. 'admin', 'retailer', 'customer'). 
 * 
 * Key relationships: users, organizations (optional).
 * Special behaviors: names/codes unique per org (composite uniqueness).
 * 
 * @namespace Core
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type roles = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$rolesPayload>
/**
 * Model sessions
 * [User Session Entity] - Implements authentication/session management for security and compliance. 
 * 
 * Tracks logins, MFA status, device fingerprints, and session validity for users. Maintains 3NF: session metadata separate from account/profile data. 
 * 
 * Key relationships: users (required).
 * Special behaviors: token is unique, enables forced logout, auditing of login locations/devices.
 * 
 * @namespace Core
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type sessions = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$sessionsPayload>
/**
 * Model locales
 * [Locale Entity] - Implements multilingual/multicultural and accessibility support, required for I18N/L10N. 
 * 
 * Defines available language/region options across platform. Maintains 3NF by centralizing locales. 
 * 
 * Key relationships: user_profiles.
 * Special behaviors: code is unique, supports expansion without refactoring user records.
 * 
 * @namespace Core
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type locales = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$localesPayload>
/**
 * Model consents
 * [Consent Entity] - Implements regulatory consent management and audit tracking for user data access, AI/ML operations, and data subject rights. 
 * 
 * Each record logs explicit user permission (for data use, AI training, communication, etc.), with retention and audit status. Maintains 3NF by storing consents independently. 
 * 
 * Key relationships: users (required).
 * Special behaviors: unique per (user, type), critical evidence for compliance and explainability.
 * 
 * @namespace Core
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type consents = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$consentsPayload>
/**
 * Model access_logs
 * [Access Log Entity] - Implements immutable, evidence-grade session/access tracking for compliance, audit, and AI/ML profiling. 3NF: links to users, sessions, and records every access event with unique context. 
 * 
 * Key relationships: users (required), sessions (optional). 
 * Special behaviors: all field values atomic and granular, no pre-aggregation; log is append-only.
 * 
 * @namespace Core
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type access_logs = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$access_logsPayload>
/**
 * Model products
 * Product entity - This implements the formal Product definition requirement from the requirements analysis. 
 * 
 * Defines a distinct, master product in the catalog. Supports lifecycle, multilingual data, AI tagging, and event evidence. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating variants, media, and relationships into normalized tables, with history/audit built via catalog_event. For example, 'Nike Air Max 2025' is a product with multiple variants, multilingual names, and tags.
 * 
 * Key relationships: variants (product_variants), categories (product_categories), media (product_media), AI tagging/relations, evidence chain (catalog_evidence).
 * Special behaviors: No calculated fields; state managed via events. Tags and categories are many-to-many via join tables.
 * 
 * @namespace ProductCatalog
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type products = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$productsPayload>
/**
 * Model product_variants
 * Product variant entity - This implements the variant granularity and stock/SKU separation requirement.
 * 
 * Represents a specific salable shape of a master product. Fully normalized (3NF) by separating each variant's attributes and price/inventory from the parent product. For example, 'Nike Air Max 2025, Size 10, Red'.
 * 
 * Key relationships: belongs to a product, links to inventory, options, and import feeds for external sync.
 * Special behaviors: No calculated fields; prices are absolute values. Tracks provenance via import_feed_id if imported.
 * 
 * @namespace ProductCatalog
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type product_variants = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$product_variantsPayload>
/**
 * Model product_categories
 * Product category entity - This implements the taxonomy and product grouping requirement.
 * 
 * Represents a single normalized category. 3NF adherence by separating parent/child via parent_id; supports multi-level category trees. Used for faceted navigation and analytics. E.g., 'Shoes', 'Sneakers', 'Men's Running'.
 * 
 * Key relationships: parent/child self-reference, mapping to products (many-to-many) via join table.
 * Special behaviors: Cannot be deleted if in use (application-level rule).
 * 
 * @namespace ProductCatalog
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type product_categories = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$product_categoriesPayload>
/**
 * Model product_options
 * Product option entity - Implements products' option normalization requirement.
 * 
 * Represents a single specifiable option (e.g., color, size) for use in variants. Maintains full 3NF by keeping every atomic choice as a separate record, variants reference these options. For example: 'Color: Red', 'Size: 10'.
 * 
 * Key relationships: many-to-many with product_variants via join table, belongs to a product.
 * Special behaviors: Option values are language-agnostic and referenced. No calculated in-option fields.
 * 
 * @namespace ProductCatalog
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type product_options = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$product_optionsPayload>
/**
 * Model product_tags
 * Product tag entity - This implements the tagging requirement, supporting extensible and AI-generated tags for search/discovery.
 *

### `users`

[User Account Entity] - This implements the secure, scalable, privacy-first user management requirement from the User & Identity Management module. 

Provides foundational identities for the platform. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating identity from profile, session, and permissions. For example, links to user events, access logs, consents, and profiles. 

Key relationships: user_profiles, sessions, consents, access_logs, roles, organizations.
Special behaviors: usernames/emails are unique, secure credential storage, full traceability and audit logging.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each user.
- `organization_id`: Belonged organization's [organizations.id](#organizations). Used for multi-tenancy and B2B relationships.
- `role_id`: Belonged role's [roles.id](#roles). Assigns user to a role for RBAC.
- `username`: [Username] - User-selected or system-generated unique username. Implements secure, unique identity requirement. For login and referencing across modules. Ensures normalization by not duplicating emails/names. Example: 'john_smith'. Unique per system.
- `email`: [Email Address] - Primary communication and login identifier. Implements secure user recovery and notification flow requirement. Must be unique. Example: 'user@example.com'.
- `phone`: [Phone Number] - Optional phone, for multi-factor authentication or contact. Implements inclusive, multi-channel communication. Can be null for email-only accounts.
- `password_hash`: [Hashed Password] - Stores strong password hash. Implements credential protection. Ensures normalization by storing only the hash (not credentials themselves) here. Never exposed via APIs.
- `is_active`: [Active Status] - Whether the account is currently enabled. Implements account lifecycle management and compliance. Disabled users cannot login or perform actions. For suspension, GDPR right-to-block, etc.
- `created_at`: [Created Timestamp] - User creation date/time. Implements audit and evidence tracking requirement. Used for onboarding analytics and compliance.
- `updated_at`: [Updated Timestamp] - Last update time for the user record. Implements integrity and audit requirement. Track for change management logs.
- `deleted_at`: [Deletion Timestamp] - Soft delete field (nullable). Implements evidence preservation and GDPR/CCPA right-to-erasure protocols. Preserved for audit without exposing to regular queries.

### `user_profiles`

[User Profile Entity] - This implements the extended user attributes and multicultural/accessibility requirements. 

Contains personal information, preferences, localization, and accessibility settings, attached 1:1 to a user. Maintains 3NF by separating profile from credential and account data. Example: stores names, avatars, language, timezone, accessibility options. 

Key relationships: users (required), locales (optional).
Special behaviors: Only one profile per user, enforces privacy segregation from authentication data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique profile record.
- `user_id`: Belonged user's [users.id](#users). 1:1 with users for privacy and structure.
- `locale_id`: Linked locale's [locales.id](#locales). Assigns preferred language/region to user.
- `full_name`: [Full Name] - Implements user's display identity requirement. For greetings, notification, and accessibility. Can be null if user prefers pseudonymity. Not duplicated elsewhere (3NF compliant). Example: 'Jane Doe'.
- `avatar_url`: [Avatar URI] - User's avatar/profile image URI. Implements personalization and a11y requirement. Example: 'https://...'
- `timezone`: [Timezone] - User's timezone code/setting. Ensures correct time display throughout platform. Implements accessibility and multicultural flow. Example: 'Asia/Seoul'.
- `bio`: [Bio] - Optional short biography or profile info for personalization. Implements user engagement. May be null. Example: 'Brand marketer and cat lover.'
- `a11y_prefs`: [Accessibility Preferences] - Stores serialized config for accessibility (screen reader, high contrast, etc). Implements accessibility compliance. 3NF: Not duplicated in any other place. Null if not set.
- `created_at`: [Created Timestamp] - Profile creation date/time. Evidence and audit. For analytics, onboarding timelines, and compliance.
- `updated_at`: [Updated Timestamp] - Last update to this profile. Audit trail and compliance.

### `organizations`

[Organization Entity] - This implements the multi-tenancy and B2B compliance requirement. 

Represents a logical business or retailer, to whom users, roles, resources may belong. Maintains 3NF: organization details are not repeated elsewhere. Supports future expansion for B2B, partner, and omnichannel flows. 

Key relationships: users, roles. 
Special behaviors: names/codes are unique within system.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique org record.
- `name`: [Organization Name] - The display/legal name for this org. Enforces multi-tenancy boundaries. Example: 'Acme Corp'. Unique system-wide.
- `code`: [Organization Code] - Short unique code/slug. Used for B2B/APIs. Example: 'ACMEC'. Ensures normalization: not repeated elsewhere. Unique.
- `created_at`: [Created Timestamp] - Org creation date/time. Audit, analytics, compliance.
- `updated_at`: [Updated Timestamp] - Last update to record. Audit and compliance.

### `roles`

[Role Entity] - Implements RBAC requirement for user access and multi-tenant permissioning. 3NF by separating roles from users. 

Defines named permission sets assignable to users (e.g. 'admin', 'retailer', 'customer'). 

Key relationships: users, organizations (optional).
Special behaviors: names/codes unique per org (composite uniqueness).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `organization_id`: Belonged organization's [organizations.id](#organizations). Allows role scoping.
- `name`: [Role Name] - Human-readable display name for the role. Example: 'admin', 'editor', 'customer'. Unique per org. Not duplicated in user records (3NF).
- `code`: [Role Code] - Machine code/slug. Used in policies/APIs. Example: 'ADMIN'. Unique per org.
- `description`: [Role Description] - Explanation of permissions/responsibilities. Used in admin UI. Example: 'Super administrator with all rights.'
- `created_at`: [Created Timestamp] - Record creation time. Evidence, audit, analytics.
- `updated_at`: [Updated Timestamp] - Last update to record. Compliance, change history.

### `sessions`

[User Session Entity] - Implements authentication/session management for security and compliance. 

Tracks logins, MFA status, device fingerprints, and session validity for users. Maintains 3NF: session metadata separate from account/profile data. 

Key relationships: users (required).
Special behaviors: token is unique, enables forced logout, auditing of login locations/devices.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique session ID.
- `user_id`: Belonged user's [users.id](#users). Session always tied to a single user.
- `token`: [Session Token] - Opaque token identifying current session (may be JWT or random). Not user credential. Unique per session, never duplicated. Used for cookie/API authentication.
- `expires_at`: [Expiration] - Timestamp this session expires. Used for timeout/logout. Enforces compliance (GDPR) and security (idle timeout).
- `device_fingerprint`: [Device Fingerprint] - Optional device identifier for fraud prevention/MFA. Supports AI-driven risk flagging. Null if unknown device.
- `ip`: [IP Address] - Last known IP address (logins/requests). Used for analytics and fraud detection. May be IPv4 or v6.
- `created_at`: [Created Timestamp] - When session was created. For session analytics, compliance, and security logging.
- `revoked_at`: [Revocation Timestamp] - Soft delete for session termination/logouts/compromised. Audit, compliance. Null if active.

### `locales`

[Locale Entity] - Implements multilingual/multicultural and accessibility support, required for I18N/L10N. 

Defines available language/region options across platform. Maintains 3NF by centralizing locales. 

Key relationships: user_profiles.
Special behaviors: code is unique, supports expansion without refactoring user records.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique locale record.
- `code`: [Locale Code] - BCP 47 code for locale/language-region. Example: 'en-US', 'ko-KR'. Used for runtime and user preference mapping. Not duplicated elsewhere. Unique.
- `name`: [Locale Name] - Human display name, e.g., 'English (United States)'. Used in UIs and reporting. Not duplicated (3NF).

### `consents`

[Consent Entity] - Implements regulatory consent management and audit tracking for user data access, AI/ML operations, and data subject rights. 

Each record logs explicit user permission (for data use, AI training, communication, etc.), with retention and audit status. Maintains 3NF by storing consents independently. 

Key relationships: users (required).
Special behaviors: unique per (user, type), critical evidence for compliance and explainability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique consent record.
- `user_id`: Belonged user's [users.id](#users). Each consent is linked to a user.
- `type`: [Consent Type] - What the consent is for (e.g., 'ai_training', 'marketing', 'data_sharing'). Implements regulatory granularity and traceability. Unique per user/type.
- `is_granted`: [Is Granted] - Whether consent is currently active. Implements GDPR/CCPA protocol. Example: true for opt-in, false for opt-out.
- `granted_at`: [Granted Timestamp] - Date/time consent granted. For audit/EVIDENCE preservation.
- `revoked_at`: [Revoked Timestamp] - Date/time consent was revoked (nullable). For lifecyle tracking, right-to-forget, compliance.

### `access_logs`

[Access Log Entity] - Implements immutable, evidence-grade session/access tracking for compliance, audit, and AI/ML profiling. 3NF: links to users, sessions, and records every access event with unique context. 

Key relationships: users (required), sessions (optional). 
Special behaviors: all field values atomic and granular, no pre-aggregation; log is append-only.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique access log record.
- `user_id`: Belonged user's [users.id](#users). Required for every access event.
- `session_id`: Belonged session's [sessions.id](#sessions). Tracks which authenticated session (if any) was used for this event. Nullable for service/system access.
- `event_type`: [Event Type] - Type of access (e.g. 'login', 'logout', 'api_call'). Atomic (3NF), used for filtering/analytics.
- `ip`: [IP Address] - Originating IP of the request. Required for security analytics, fraud detection. 3NF: not duplicated in session/user, always present here.
- `agent`: [User Agent] - Client software/device string for the request. Key for security/audit analytics. This is atomic and not pre-processed; always stored in full.
- `success`: [Success Flag] - Whether the access event resulted in successful authentication or action. Key compliance/audit outcome tracker.
- `occurred_at`: [Occurred At] - Exact timestamp of the access event (UTC). Preserved for forensic/audit/analytics evidence. Never updated/overwritten (append-only log).

### `products`

Product entity - This implements the formal Product definition requirement from the requirements analysis. 

Defines a distinct, master product in the catalog. Supports lifecycle, multilingual data, AI tagging, and event evidence. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating variants, media, and relationships into normalized tables, with history/audit built via catalog_event. For example, 'Nike Air Max 2025' is a product with multiple variants, multilingual names, and tags.

Key relationships: variants (product_variants), categories (product_categories), media (product_media), AI tagging/relations, evidence chain (catalog_evidence).
Special behaviors: No calculated fields; state managed via events. Tags and categories are many-to-many via join tables.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Globally unique product identifier.
- `created_by_user_id`: Creator's user [users.id](#users). Maintains authorship, compliance, and access tracking.
- `updated_by_user_id`: Last updater's user [users.id](#users). Maintains modification tracking and audit compliance.
- `name`
  > Product canonical name - Implements the core product naming requirement.
  >
  > Atomic field, supports primary search/display. Eg: 'Apple iPhone 23'. Normalized (no composite names).
- `description`
  > Localized/language-variant product description. Represents main product overview.
  >
  > Supports i18n by being atomic; per-language splits handled in separate table if needed. Eg: short English/long Korean text.
- `internal_code`
  > Internal code/identifier for supply chain tracking (SKU-less, human-readable).
  >
  > Fully atomic value, no lookups. Eg: 'PROD-2025-AX1'.
- `status`
  > Logical product state (draft, active, suspended, archived) - Implements state machine requirement.
  >
  > Atomic value used for workflow/status handling. Eg: 'active'. No transitive dependencies.
- `created_at`
  > Creation timestamp. Implements data logging, compliance, catalog event lifecycle.
  >
  > Atomic. Not calculated; audit enforced via event log.
- `updated_at`: Most recent update timestamp. Audit/compliance/log requirement. Atomic and independent of other fields.

### `product_variants`

Product variant entity - This implements the variant granularity and stock/SKU separation requirement.

Represents a specific salable shape of a master product. Fully normalized (3NF) by separating each variant's attributes and price/inventory from the parent product. For example, 'Nike Air Max 2025, Size 10, Red'.

Key relationships: belongs to a product, links to inventory, options, and import feeds for external sync.
Special behaviors: No calculated fields; prices are absolute values. Tracks provenance via import_feed_id if imported.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique variant identifier.
- `product_id`: Parent product's [products.id](#products) - Enforces variant dependence.
- `import_feed_id`: Import source feed's [import_feeds.id](#import_feeds). For data provenance, nullable if direct.
- `sku`: SKU for the variant (external or internal) - Implements inventory and supply chain reference, atomic per variant.
- `price`
  > Unit price for the stock-keeping unit; monetary value in store currency.
  >
  > No pre-calculation, represents current/active price only.
- `barcode`: Retail barcode or EAN for regulatory scan/stock management. Atomic, not combined.
- `available`: Denotes if variant is enabled for sale. Atomic flag, not calculated.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of variant creation. Supports event/audit compliance, atomic value.
- `updated_at`: Last modification of the variant; atomic, tracked for compliance.

### `product_categories`

Product category entity - This implements the taxonomy and product grouping requirement.

Represents a single normalized category. 3NF adherence by separating parent/child via parent_id; supports multi-level category trees. Used for faceted navigation and analytics. E.g., 'Shoes', 'Sneakers', 'Men's Running'.

Key relationships: parent/child self-reference, mapping to products (many-to-many) via join table.
Special behaviors: Cannot be deleted if in use (application-level rule).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique category identifier.
- `parent_id`: Parent category id [product_categories.id](#product_categories) (for hierarchy); nullable for root.
- `name`: Category display name; atomic. E.g.: 'Apparel', 'Running Shoes'.
- `created_at`: Category creation timestamp, for logging, evidence, and i18n flows.
- `updated_at`: Category update timestamp. Maintains audit/compliance.

### `product_options`

Product option entity - Implements products' option normalization requirement.

Represents a single specifiable option (e.g., color, size) for use in variants. Maintains full 3NF by keeping every atomic choice as a separate record, variants reference these options. For example: 'Color: Red', 'Size: 10'.

Key relationships: many-to-many with product_variants via join table, belongs to a product.
Special behaviors: Option values are language-agnostic and referenced. No calculated in-option fields.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique product option identifier.
- `product_id`: Owns product's [products.id](#products) - Each option is scoped to a single product.
- `option_type`: Type of option (e.g., 'color', 'size'). Atomic descriptor, no list aggregation.
- `value`: Atomic option value (e.g., 'Red', 'XL'). Single value per record; reference only.

### `product_tags`

Product tag entity - This implements the tagging requirement, supporting extensible and AI-generated tags for search/discovery.

Represents a single logical tag, maintained fully normalized (one tag per record). Used for many-to-many linking to products via a junction; enables advanced AI/ML. E.g., 'Eco-friendly', 'AI-generated: trending', '2025 Spring'.

Key relationships: many-to-many with products via join table. Not bound to product for de-dupe.
Special behaviors: Cannot be deleted if mapped to product by business rule (handled in logic, not schema).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique tag identifier.
- `value`: Atomic tag value: presented for searches, filtering, and AI workflows. Not compound fields. E.g., 'Seasonal'.
- `created_at`: Timestamp for tag creation; enables audit, compliance, and ML features.

### `product_media`

Product media entity - Implements digital asset management for products, normalization requirement for file/asset reference.

Represents a single atomic asset—image, video, PDF—linked to a product or variant. Asset metadata and localization handled at field level. Maintains normalization by not duplicating media data. E.g., 'main.jpg', 'unboxing.mp4'.

Key relationships: linked to product or product_variant, not both. Media may be globally reused via indirect links.
Special behaviors: File content is reference only (URI), not stored in DB.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique asset identifier.
- `product_id`: Linked product's [products.id](#products). Exactly one of product_id or product_variant_id must be non-null.
- `product_variant_id`: Linked product variant's [product_variants.id](#product_variants). Enforces exclusivity, one of two FK must be set.
- `uri`: Atomic URI to remote asset (never stores blobs in DB).
- `media_type`: Type of asset ('image', 'video', etc).
- `locale`: Locale/region of this asset, per i18n/a11y. E.g.: 'ko-KR'.
- `alt_text`: Accessibility alt text for asset, complying with a11y WCA2.
- `created_at`: Asset creation timestamp; audit/evidence field, 3NF.

### `inventory`

Inventory entity - Implements core inventory tracking and evidence preservation requirement.

Represents a normalized, atomic inventory record for product variants. No aggregate or pre-computed stock. Maintains 3NF by keeping each update/event in a separate record (history by design). For example: inventory for 'Nike Air Max 2025, Size 10'.

Key relationships: One-to-one links with product_variant; ties to evidence/events for audit. 
Special behaviors: never calculates stock at DB layer—only raw stock updates and absolute counts.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique inventory record identifier.
- `product_variant_id`: Tracked variant's [product_variants.id](#product_variants). Each inventory maps to exactly one variant.
- `stock_count`: Current available quantity of the variant, stored as absolute number. No pre-calculation or aggregate fields (only most recent state, all log/events via catalog_event).
- `last_modified_at`: Last update time to this inventory; compliance and event tracking, atomic.

### `import_feeds`

Import feed entity - Implements catalog import normalization and data provenance requirement.

Represents an atomic, external data feed used for catalog enrichment/import tracking. Maintains 3NF, links each imported product/variant via foreign key. For example: Google Shopping product import, partner ERP feed.

Key relationships: product_variant is mapped to a single import_feed.
Special behaviors: mutable for correction, immutable evidence via catalog_evidence. No calculated aggregate fields allowed.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique import feed identifier.
- `source_name`: Human-readable name of the import source. E.g., 'Google Shopping'.
- `source_uri`: URI of the import data source/feed; allows for evidence and provenance tracking.
- `imported_at`: Timestamp of data feed import into catalog; audit/compliance.

### `catalog_events`

Catalog event entity - Implements catalog state change logging, compliance, and evidence preservation requirement.

Represents an immutable, atomic event: product/variant creation, change, import, status update, etc. Maintains strict normalization (no denormalized rollup in this table), links to evidence and actors. For example: a price update event for a variant.

Key relationships: links user (actor), product or variant, optional evidence pointer.
Special behaviors: Chronological, append-only; never updated/deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique event identifier.
- `product_id`: Target product's [products.id](#products). Nullable, may target variant instead.
- `product_variant_id`: Target variant's [product_variants.id](#product_variants). Nullable if product-level event.
- `user_id`: Responsible actor's [users.id](#users) (who performed the event).
- `event_type`: Type of event (e.g., creation, update, import, deletion, status_change, etc). Atomic category (not compound).
- `description`: Detailed description of event for compliance/evidence. Atomic; not calculated.
- `occurred_at`: Atomic timestamp of event occurrence. Preserves chronological evidence and supports full audit trail.

### `catalog_evidence`

Catalog evidence entity - Implements immutable evidence preservation requirement for all critical catalog actions/events per compliance rules.

Represents a single, atomic evidence/log record attached to an event: file links, signature, or raw snapshot URI. Maintains strict normalization; links to catalog_event or catalog-related entity. For example: file hash of import, signed docs for regulatory purposes.

Key relationships: links to at most one catalog_event, may be referenced by compliance/external audit logic.
Special behaviors: Direct evidence content never stored; only signed reference/URI.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique evidence identifier.
- `catalog_event_id`: Target event's [catalog_events.id](#catalog_events). Each evidence strictly linked to one event per 3NF, nullable for external evidence.
- `reference_uri`: Atomic URI (file, s3, IPFS, hash url, etc) to external evidence; never locally stored blobs.
- `description`: Atomic evidence description for traceability and legal compliance.
- `created_at`: Evidence creation timestamp; 3NF compliance, chronological audit.

### `cart`

[Cart management] - This implements the requirement for intelligent, audit-preserving cart management from the 'Intelligent Cart and Order Processing Requirements Specification'.

This model represents a user's persistent cart, maintaining strict data integrity, full auditability, session support, and secure linkage to user or session. It ensures 3NF normalization by keeping only atomic and essential cart-level data; item-level details reside in cart_item. Example: recovering a user's cart across multiple devices or after authentication.

Key relationships: references user, session, and cart_item models for ownership, context, and item containment.
Special behaviors: Cart identity is unique; maintains only normalized relations, all item data tracked via junction table.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Identifies each cart instance uniquely.
- `user_id`
  > Belonged user's [users.id](#users)
  > The primary account associated with this cart; enables cart persistence across devices and sessions.
- `session_id`
  > Associated session's [sessions.id](#sessions)
  > Optional. Associates anonymous/pre-login carts; provides seamless upgrade upon login.
- `created_at`: [Cart creation timestamp] - Implements evidence and regulatory requirements. Used for audit logging, recovery, and analytics. Ensures normalization by tracking atomic event only. Ex: '2025-06-10T04:59:24' when cart first initiated.
- `updated_at`: [Cart update timestamp] - Implements traceability and audit requirements, storing only atomic last-changed value. Allows tracking of recent activity. Ex: '2025-06-10T05:03:45' after a product added.
- `deleted_at`: [Soft deletion timestamp] - Implements compliance, right-to-be-forgotten, and data integrity requirements. Null if active, set on removal for evidence trail. Ex: null for active, timestamp for deleted cart.

### `cart_item`

[Cart item detail] - This implements the requirement for normalized, auditable cart item management from the 'Intelligent Cart and Order Processing Requirements Specification'.

Represents each item in a user's cart, maintaining full normalization (3NF). Item quantities, variant choice, and intent are recorded atomically. Auditability is ensured by timestamping and separate evidence models where required. Example: when a user adds three units of a size-M, green T-shirt variant to cart.

Key relationships: references cart, product_variant for linkage; product reference maintained via product_variant only. No calculated data; all denormalization only in views.
Special behaviors: One cart_item per variant per cart; unique constraint enforced.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies this cart-item record.
- `cart_id`
  > Parent cart's [cart.id](#cart)
  > Links this item to the cart that holds it.
- `product_variant_id`
  > Product variant's [product_variants.id](#product_variants)
  > Links to the specific SKU/configuration the user intends to buy.
- `quantity`: [Quantity desired] - Implements cart quantity requirements. Stores atomic, user-specified intent. Ex: '3' for three items of the variant.
- `added_at`: [Item addition timestamp] - Serves evidence and analytics needs. Timestamp for when specific item added to cart. Ex: '2025-06-10T04:59:24'.
- `updated_at`: [Last update timestamp] - Tracks modification; e.g. quantity update. Normalized (not derived) atomic history. Ex: '2025-06-10T05:00:00'.

### `order`

[Order lifecycle record] - Implements the requirement for normalized, robust, evidence-preserving order process management from the requirements specification.

Each order record represents a unique commerce transaction, including linkage to user, cart, payment, and state tracking. Strict 3NF assures no duplication—order_items contain line-level details. All status/history/evidence handled via related tables. Example: new purchase by user, tracked through all subsequent states (placed, shipped, completed).

Key relationships: references user, cart, payment and state-tracking models for full join capability.
Special behaviors: Atomic values only (total, status, etc. never pre-calculated). Order evidence and logs stored externally for compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique ID per order transaction.
- `user_id`
  > Ordering user's [users.id](#users)
  > Links order to user account for audit and analytics.
- `cart_id`
  > Source cart's [cart.id](#cart)
  > Links to the cart used to place this order. Enables full evidence chain for compliance.
- `created_at`: [Order creation timestamp] - Required by audit, compliance, and analytics. Atomic, strictly non-duplicated event. E.g., '2025-06-10T04:59:24'.
- `updated_at`: [Order update timestamp] - Captures atomic change events for evidence and operational review. E.g., '2025-06-10T05:30:00'.
- `deleted_at`: [Soft delete marker] - For compliance and historic evidence, set if order is voided/cancelled; otherwise null. Never physically deleted.

### `order_item`

[Order line-level detail] - Implements the requirement for strictly normalized, traceable order item management.

Represents each SKU/configuration in an order, recording atomic quantity and reference to product_variant. Ensures full 3NF by detaching all calculations, price, or analytic rollup. All audit trails and evidence for each action reside in related tables. Example: order includes 2 blue jeans, variant #7.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for line item.
- `order_id`
  > Parent order's [order.id](#order)
  > Links to the order containing this line item.
- `product_variant_id`
  > Product variant's [product_variants.id](#product_variants)
  > Spell out the line as describing which exact stock-keeping unit.
- `quantity`: [Ordered quantity] - Stores user-purchased units. Ensures atomic, normalized order content. E.g., user orders 2 of variant #7.
- `added_at`: [Addition to order timestamp] - For evidence and tracking requirements. Details time when item became part of order. E.g., '2025-06-10T04:59:24'.
- `updated_at`: [Update timestamp] - For last atomic update to line item details. For event logging. E.g., '2025-06-10T05:04:03'.

### `order_status`

[Order status tracking] - Implements normalized, evidence-enabled order lifecycle state management as required for audit, analytics, and compliance.

Each record logs a status transition for an order, rather than storing 'latest' status inline. Full history of order state is tracked as a sequence by timestamps. Example: 'pending', 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered'.

Key relationships: references order for parent linkage.
Special behaviors: No denormalization; only atomic status per row. Materialized views to hold summary/latest states.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. One per status change event.
- `order_id`
  > Target order's [order.id](#order)
  > Defines which order this status record is about.
- `status_code`: [Order status code] - Represents atomic order state (e.g., 'pending', 'paid', 'shipped'). Compliance: values are strictly controlled by system logic or enumeration.
- `changed_at`: [Status change timestamp] - Implements complete event history. Atomic per change. E.g., '2025-06-10T05:12:09'.
- `changed_by`: [Status changer] - For evidence and audit, identifies the user or system actor triggering the state change. Links to user.id or reserved system id. Null if system-automated.

### `order_log`

[Order event logging] - Implements the requirement for immutable, tamper-evident record of all material order-related actions.

Each record logs an event (e.g., creation, update, state transition, evidence attachment) for an order, including timestamps and relevant actor info. All analytics, AI-driven detection, and compliance evidence are sourced from this log. Full 3NF compliance is achieved—no calculated or summary fields.

Key relationships: references target order; may reference evidence where applicable.
Special behaviors: Immutable logs; complete itemization (no aggregations within table).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key for log entry.
- `order_id`
  > Target order's [order.id](#order)
  > Order event relates to this specific transaction.
- `evidence_id`
  > Linked evidence's [order_evidence.id](#order_evidence)
  > Optional; logs external file or digital signature as audit evidence for this event.
- `event_type`: [Event type] - Type or category of event; e.g., 'create', 'update', 'status_change', 'attach_evidence'. Normalized, not pre-calculated. Used for filtering, audit, analytics.
- `event_description`: [Event detail] - Atomic description, not derived or aggregated. E.g., 'Order was shipped via courier'.
- `event_time`: [Event timestamp] - Exact time when event occurred; essential for evidence compliance and analytics.
- `actor_id`: [Event actor] - User ID or system actor responsible for event. Used in compliance analysis. Null if unauthenticated or system auto-action.

### `order_evidence`

[Order evidence registry] - Satisfies requirement to record all compliance, audit or dispute evidence associated with order operations.

Holds atomic pointers to files, digital receipts, or cryptographic proof objects related to a specific order. Evidence records are separate for full normalization. Example: PDF invoice, delivery photo, digital signature pertaining to an order.

Key relationships: links order and potentially the user or system actor providing the evidence.
Special behaviors: Only atomic and external reference fields allowed; all denormalization in materialized view.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key for evidence record.
- `order_id`
  > Associated order's [order.id](#order)
  > Defines which order this evidence relates to.
- `evidence_type`: [Evidence type] - Type of evidence (e.g., 'invoice', 'signature', 'photo', 'receipt'). Normalized, strictly conformance for evidence audit. E.g., 'invoice'.
- `evidence_uri`: [Evidence URI] - URI/location to external asset or file. Atomic, not aggregated. E.g., 'https://evidence.bucket/signed-invoice.pdf'.
- `provided_at`: [Provided timestamp] - When the evidence was recorded into the system. Serves compliance and analytics. E.g., '2025-06-10T06:09:00'.
- `provided_by`: [Provider/actor reference] - User or third-party id responsible for provision. For traceability, audit and compliance. Null if system-automated.
